source: V říjnu 2016 vyšlo album You Want it Darker, na kterém Cohen spolupracoval se svým synem Adamem. Poprosil ho, aby mu pomohl jednotlivé písně dokončit. Na intimní nahrávce se Cohen symbolicky vyrovná s blížící se smrtí. Zemřel měsíc po vydání alba ve věku 82 let.

source: Z knihovny Václava IV. se nezachovala na českém území ani jedna kniha. Tato knihovna patřila podle odborníků k nejrozsáhlejším a také nejkrásnějším knižním sbírkám v tehdejší střední Evropě, protože mladý král toužil po vybudování reprezentativní knihovny, která by se vyrovnala knižním sbírkám jeho francouzských příbuzných. Knihovna však zanikla brzy po Václavově smrti. Podle všeho byla rozkradena nebo zničena při dobývání hradu husity. Několik kodexů ale bylo zachráněno. Nejvíce jich dnes vlastní Rakouská národní knihovna.
reference: No books from Wenceslas IV's library survived in the Czech Republic. According to experts, the library used to have one of the largest and most beautiful book collections in Central Europe in those times, the result of the young King's desire to have a highly presentable library that would compare to the book collections of his French relatives. However, the library perished soon after Wenceslas's death. It is most likely that it was ransacked or destroyed when the castle was besieged by the Hussites. A few codices were saved, most of which are now owned by the Austrian National Library.

source: I don't believe de Grood should ever be unsupervised permanently. A parole-like system where he has to check in to make sure he's still taking his medication could work well. Arguing that he or other mentally ill people remain institutionalized unless absolutely necessary is a form of segregation. It perpetuates the idea that mentally ill people, those with schizophrenia in particular, cannot ever mesh with society; thus continuing the stigma and perpetuating the idea that they are dangerous criminals. He was found not criminally responsible by a court of law, so why should he be treated like a prisoner instead of someone who was ill and is now better?
reference: Věřím, že není nutné, aby byl de Grood stále pod trvalým dozorem. Systém podmínečného propuštění, ve kterém se musí hlásit, abychom měli jistotu, že stále bere léky, by mohl dobře fungovat. Argument, že on nebo další duševně nemocní lidé mají zůstat v ústavní péči, pokud to není nezbytně nutné, je formou segregace. Zachovává představu, že duševně nemocní lidé, zejména lidé trpící schizofrenií, nikdy nemohou dobře zapadnout do společnosti; tak pokračuje stigmatizace nemocných a udržuje se společenský názor, že jsou to nebezpeční zločinci. Soud de Grooda shledal trestně odpovědným, tak proč by s ním mělo být zacházeno jako s vězněm místo s někým, kdo je nemocný a jehož zdravotní stav se nyní zlepšil?

source: Interestingly, one of the 12 galaxies in z66OD was a giant object with a huge body of gas, known as Himiko, which was found previously by the Subaru Telescope in 2009. "It is reasonable to find a protocluster near a massive object, such as Himiko. However, we're surprised to see that Himiko was located not in the center of the protocluster, but on the edge 500 million light-years away from the center." said Masami Ouchi, a team member at the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan and the University of Tokyo, who discovered Himiko in 2009. Ironically, the mythological queen Himiko is also said to have lived cloistered away from her people. Ouchi continues, "It is still not understood why Himiko is not located in the center. These results will be a key for understanding the relationship between clusters and massive galaxies."
reference: Interessanterweise war eine der 12 Galaxien in z66OD ein gigantisches Objekt mit einem riesigen Gaskörper, das unter dem Namen Himiko bekannt ist und das bereits 2009 vom Subaru-Teleskop gefunden wurde. „Es ist zu erwarten, dass man ein Protocluster in der Nähe eines riesigen Objekts wie Himiko findet. Uns überrascht jedoch, dass sich Himiko nicht im Zentrum des Protoclusters befand, sondern am Rand, etwa 500 Millionen Lichtjahre vom Zentrum entfernt“, berichtete Masami Ouchi, ein Mitglied des Teams des nationalen astronomischen Observatoriums von Japan und der Universität Tokio, das Himiko im Jahr 2009 entdeckt hatte. Ironischerweise soll die mythologische Königin Himiko ebenfalls zurückgezogen fernab ihres Volkes gelebt haben. Ouchi erklärt weiter: „Wir verstehen immer noch nicht, warum Himiko sich nicht im Zentrum befindet. Diese Ergebnisse werden uns helfen, die Beziehung zwischen Galaxienhaufen und riesigen Galaxien zu verstehen.

source: The environmental problems addressed by Cullis-Suzuki reflect the world of the early 1990s, when deforestation, the depletion of the ozone layer, and the extinction of species were the ecological concerns de jour. Yet humanity has been fairly successful at resolving those problems in the intervening years. Thanks to a landmark chemicals ban, ozone depletion has slowed dramatically, and forest cover worldwide has increased by an area the size of Texas and Alaska combined.
reference: Die Umweltprobleme, die von Cullis-Suzuki angesprochen werden, spiegeln die Welt der frühen 1990er wider, in der die Abholzung, der Abbau der Ozonschicht sowie das Artensterben die ökologischen Sorgen darstellten. Dennoch war die Menschheit in den darauffolgenden Jahren recht erfolgreich im Lösen dieser Probleme. Dank eines bahnbrechenden Verbots von Chemikalien konnte der Abbau der Ozonschicht drastisch verlangsamt werden und die Waldbedeckung weltweit hat um die Fläche Texas und Alaskas insgesamt zugenommen.

source: La contrefaçon de produits médicaux et les infractions similaires constituent une forme de criminalité grave, qui menace la santé des êtres humains en raison de dosages insuffisants ou même de l’absence de substances actives s’agissant de médicaments, ou de matériaux défectueux pour ce qui est des dispositifs médicaux (prothèses, implants cardiaques, etc.).
reference: Il Consiglio federale aveva deciso in merito nel giugno 2011. La contraffazione di medicamenti e reati simili sono una forma di criminalità grave, che mette in serio pericolo la salute umana. Nel caso di medicamenti, a causa di dosaggi insufficienti o persino di assenza dei principi attivi; nel caso di dispositivi medici (protesi, impianti cardiaci, ecc.), a causa di materiali scadenti.
translation: Il Consiglio federale aveva deciso in merito nel giugno 2011. source: Laut den Forschern ist die Temperatur für die Haltbarkeit von Akkus ein entscheidender Faktor. Da spielt jedes einzelne Grad eine Rolle. Beim Laden mit höheren Temperaturen buße die Batterie nicht nur an Kapazität ein, sondern sie halte auch insgesamt nicht so lange durch. Die Lebensdauer fällt also geringer aus. Die Forscher raten deshalb dazu, das Smartphone stets per Kabel aufzuladen. Da ein Akkutausch bei modernen Smartphones stets mit hohen Kosten verbunden ist, dürfte das ein hilfreicher Tipp sein. Apple hat zuletzt die Kosten für einen Akkutausch sogar noch einmal erhöht - und zwar für alle iPhones.
reference: According to the scientists, temperature is a deciding factor for the durability of batteries. Every single degree is relevant. When charging at higher temperatures, the battery not only loses capacity but also durability. Its service life is therefore shorter. Thus, the scientists recommend that smartphones should always be charged via cable. Since replacing the battery in modern smartphones is always quite expensive, this should be a helpful tip. Apple has recently increased the cost of battery replacement for all iPhone models.

source: Berechnungen des Ökonomen Dan Alpert von der Cornell Law School in New York zufolge mietete WeWork in Manhatten, einem der teuersten Immobilienmärkte der Welt, in den vergangenen 24 Monaten knapp 300.000 Quadratmeter Bürofläche an. Allein WeWorks Neuverträge sorgten dafür, dass die Nachfrage nach Büros in New York größer war als die in dieser Zeit neu auf den Markt gekommenen Flächen. Ohne WeWorks Expansion wäre der Büro-Leerstand in der US-Metropole in dieser Zeit gestiegen, wie Alpert im "Business Insider" schrieb. Ähnlich sieht es in London aus, wo WeWork inzwischen mehrere Dutzend Bürostandorte in bester Lage betreibt.
reference: According to calculations by the economist Dan Alpert from Cornell Law School in New York, during the past 24 months WeWork has rented almost 300,000 square meters of office space in Manhattan, one of the most expensive property markets in the world. WeWork’s new contracts alone caused a demand for offices in New York that was higher than all the new space coming onto the market during this period. As written by Alpert in Business Insider, without WeWork’s expansion, the amount of empty office space in the US metropolis would have risen during this period. The situation is similar in London, where in the meantime WeWork runs several dozen office locations in top areas.

reference: For his "campaign for a sustainable and respectful use of the world's seas," the polar explorer from Bad Bramstedt received the Seadevcon Maritime Award during Hamburg Climate Week. source: Eigentlich hatte sich Premier Boris Johnson eindeutig festgelegt: Mit ihm wird es einen dritten Aufschub der Brexit-Verhandlungen garantiert nicht geben. Aber welche Aussagen sind beim polarisierenden Briten schon von ewiger Dauer. Das jüngste Urteil des Obersten Gerichtes in Großbritanniens schwebt wie ein Damoklesschwert über dem Blondschopf. Seine Suspendierung des Parlaments, um seinen Brexit-Kurs bis zum Austrittsdatum stur durchführen zu können, wurde Anfang dieser Woche annulliert. Und ein vom Parlament verabschiedetes Gesetz verpflichtet Johnson dazu, im Falle gescheiterter Verhandlungen mit der EU bis zum 31. Oktober eine Verlängerung der bilateralen Gespräche zu bewirken. Das hatte Johnson jedoch kategorisch immer wieder ausgeschlossen.
reference: Originally, Prime Minister Boris Johnson had committed himself: there would be no third delay in the Brexit negotiations. But which statements by the polarizing Briton have stood the test of time? The latest ruling of the Supreme Court of the United Kingdom hangs over the towhead like the sword of Damocles. His suspension of parliament in order to wrestle his Brexit-course through to the exit date was annulled early this week. A law passed by parliament obligates Johnson to bring about an extension of the bilateral talks in the case of failed negotiations with the EU by October 31st. This has always been categorically ruled out by Johnson.

A law passed by parliament obligates Johnson to bring about an extension of the bilateral talks in the case of failed negotiations with the EU by October 31st. This has always been categorically ruled out by Johnson.

source: Doch bevor es so weit ist, können die Astronomen ihn eingehend beobachten. Denn im Gegensatz zu seinem Vorgänger ist 2I/Borisov bereits in seinem Anflug gesichtet worden, was bedeutet, dass er viele Monate lang von der Erde aus untersucht werden kann. "Das Objekt wird Mitte Dezember die größte Helligkeit erreichen und dann noch bis April 2020 mit mittelgroßen Teleskopen zu sehen sein", erklärt Davide Farnocchia von der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa. "Danach wird es bis Oktober 2020 nur noch mit größeren, professionellen Teleskopen zu beobachten sein".
reference: But before it gets to that stage, astronomers can watch it closely. Then in contrast to its predecessor, 2l/Borisov has already been sighted before its approach, which means that it can be examined from earth for many months to come. "The object will reach its greatest brightness by mid-December and will then still be visible through medium-sized telescopes until April 2020," Davide Farnocchia of the Nasa US space agency explains. "After that it will still be visible through bigger, professional telescopes until October 2020."

source: Vergangenes Wochenende war es in Kairo, Alexandria, Suez und Mansura zu Protesten mit Hunderten Teilnehmern gekommen. Sie richteten sich gegen die Regierung von Präsident Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, dem Kritiker Korruption und Misswirtschaft vorwerfen. Einen so offenen Protest gegen die politische Führung hatte es in Ägypten seit Jahren nicht gegeben. Der im spanischen Exil lebende ägyptische Bauunternehmer und Schauspieler Mohammed Ali, der die Demonstrationen mit Video-Botschaften auf Facebook ins Rollen brachte, hat für den heutigen Freitag zu einem "Millionenmarsch" an zentralen Plätzen im Land aufgerufen. Ali fordert eine "Volksrevolution". Der Mann ist für die meisten jungen Ägypter zwar auch kein "Guter, weil er als Subunternehmer für die Armee Millionen scheffelte, aber seine Botschaften kommen an.
reference: Protests with hundreds of participants took place in Cairo, Alexandria, Suez, and Mansoura over the past weekend. They were aimed at the government of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, who is being accused of corruption and mismanagement. There has been no such open protest against the political leadership in Egypt in years. Mohammed Ali, an Egyptian developer and actor who lives in exile in Spain, set off the protests with video messages on Facebook and called for a march of millions on central plazas in the country. Ali demanded a People’s revolution. Although not considered “one of the good guys” by most young Egyptians because he earned millions as a subcontractor for the army, his messages have reach.

translation: It was announced in the central budget on the 5th of last July, that using the Aadhar number instead of the PAN number when filing income tax would be sufficient.

source: உலக அளவில் உயிரிழப்புக்கான முக்கிய காரணிகளில் மாரடைப்பு உள்ளிட்ட இதய நோய்கள் முதலிடத்தில் உள்ளன என்று இதய அறுவை சிகிச்சை நிபுணர் மருத்துவர் ஜி. செங்கோட்டுவேலு தெரிவித்தார்.

source: சமுதாயத்தில் தொழில் நுட்ப கல்வி, மதிப்புகள் மற்றும் தர்மம், தர்மமும் சிறந்த வாழ்க்கை முறையும், நிழல்படம், காணொளி எடுத்து ஆவணப்படுத்துதல் என 32 பாடங்கள் அந்த பட்டியலில் இடம் பெற்றுள்ளன.

translation: The list had 32 subjects such as Technical education in society, Values and ethics, Ethics and best lifestyle, Documentation of Photos and videos.

source: இதில், 85 வயது மூதாட்டியும் தேர்ச்சி பெற்றுள்ளார்.

translation: An 85 year old elderly woman has also passed in this exam.

translation: In his lecture in the seminar he said the campaign of BJP mentioning One Nation, One culture, one election, and one education system has questioned the plurality of India.

source: இந்த ஹோட்டலின் சமையற்கலைஞர்கள் இணைந்து 101 உணவுகளை தயார்செய்து காட்சிக்கு வைத்திருந்தனர்.

translation: That check dam built in Mayanur has improved the ground water level in that area.

translation: Upon inquiry, it was revealed that all the ambulances were used for the filming of the new film directed by Pon Ram starring actor Sasikumar.

source: அயோத்தி வழக்கில் அக்டோபர் 18-ம் தேதிக்குள் வாதங்களை முடிக்க வேண்டும் என மீண்டும் சுட்டிக் காட்டிய நீதிபதிகள், அதற்கேற்ப இந்து மற்றும் முஸ்லிம் தரப்புகள் தங்கள் வாதங்களை முடிப்பதற்கான கால அளவை குறிப்பிட வேண்டும் என தெரிவித்தனர்.

translation: The judges pointed out that the arguments need to be completed by October 18 and accordingly, the Hindu and Islamic sides need to specify the time period to complete their arguments.

source: இந்நிலை யில், நாசாவின் எல்ஆர்ஓசி ஆர்பிட்டர் கடந்த 17ஆம் தேதி நிலவின் தென் துருவ பகுதியை கடந்து சென்றது.

translation: In this scenario, LROC orbiter of NASA crossed the South Pole region on the Moon on the 17th of last month.

source: போலீஸ் ஹாரன் சத்தத்தை கேட்டதும் மோட்டார் சைக்கிளில் வந்த 3 பேர் வண்டியை வேகமாக எடுத்துக் கொண்டு தப்பி சென்றனர்.

translation: On hearing the horn of the police the 3 persons escaped on the motor cycle in which they have come.

translation: With the permission denied, a complaint was given to the District Collector and Tirupur District Police commissioner.

source: மலுக்கு தீவுகள் பகுதியில் அமைந்துள்ள அம்போன் நகர் அருகே, வியாழக்கிழமை காலை 8.45 மணிக்கு (உள்ளூர் நேரம்) சக்தி வாய்ந்த நில நடுக்கம் ஏற்பட்டது.

translation: There was a powerful earthquake near Ambon city in Malukku islands on Thursday at 8.45 am (local time).

source: ஆனால், பெரியார் தான் பெண் கள் படிக்க வேண்டும், அவர்களது வாழ்வாதாரம் உயரவேண்டும், சொத்தில் சம உரிமை வழங்க வேண் டும் என பாடுபட்டார்.

translation: But it was only Periyar who struggled for women’s education, improvement of their livelihood and equal rights in property.

source: சிதிலமடைந்துள்ள பழைய குடியிருப்புகளை இடித்துவிட்டு புதிய குடியிருப்புகளை கட்டித்தருமாறு குடியிருப்புவாசிகளின் கோரிக்கையை ஏற்று, விரைவில் பணிகள் துவக்கப்பட்டு புதிய குடியிருப்புகள் கட்டி முடிக்கப்படும் என்று துணை முதலமைச்சர் குடியிருப்புவாசிகளுக்கு உறுதியளித்தார்.
reference: The Deputy Chief Minister assured the residents that their demand to demolish the dilapidated flats and build new ones, will be accepted and works for construction of new flats will be started soon and completed.
translation: The Deputy Chief Minister assured the residents that their demand to demolish the dilapidated flats and build new ones, will be accepted and works for construction of new flats will be started soon and completed.

source: நீட் தேர்வில் ஆள்மாறாட்டம் செய்து வெற்றிபெற்று தேனி மருத்துவக்கல்லூரியில் சேர்ந்து படிப்பதாக சென்னை மாணவன் உதித்சூர்யா மீது புகார் எழுந்தது.

translation: There was a complaint regarding a Chennai student about passing the NEET exam by impersonating and securing admission to Theni Medical College.

source: ஜனநாயக ரீதியில் கட்டுப்பாட் டோடு மதச்சார்பற்ற முற்போக்குக் கூட்டணியினர் நடத்திய ஆர்ப் பாட்டம் திருப்பூர் மக்களிடையே வன்முறைக்கு எதிரான விழிப்புணர் வைத் தோற்றுவித்தது என்றால் அது மிகையில்லை!

translation: That the protest was conducted democratically, and with control by the Secular Progressive Alliance, creating awareness against violence among the people of Tirupur, is not an overstatement!

source: வருமான வரி செலுத்தும் தனி நபருக்கும், நிறுவனத்துக்கும் நிரந்தர வருமான வரி கணக்கு எண் (பான் எண்) என்ற 10 இலக்கத்தில் எண்ணும், எழுத்தும் கொண்ட அடையாள எண்ணை வருமான வரித் துறை வழங்குகிறது.
reference: The income tax department is providing a 10 digit alphanumeric identification number called a Permanent Income Tax Account Number (PAN number) for tax paying individuals and companies.
translation: The income tax department is providing a 10 digit alphanumeric identification number called a Permanent Income Tax Account Number (PAN number) for tax paying individuals and companies.

source: கருத்தரங்கில் மார்க்சிஸ்ட் கம்யூனிஸ்ட் கட்சியின் தமிழ் மாநில செயலாளர் பாலகிருஷ்ணன், புதுச்சேரி மாநில செயலாளர் ராஜாங்கம் மற்றும் முன்னணி தலைவர்கள் கலந்துகொண்டனர்.
reference: Balakrishnan, the Tamilnadu state secretary of Marxist communist party, Pudhuchery district Secretary Rajangam and other leaders participated in the conference.
translation: Balakrishnan, the Tamilnadu state secretary of Marxist communist party, Pudhuchery district Secretary Rajangam and other leaders participated in the conference.

source: 3000 வருடங்களுக்கு முன்பாக இந்தியாவில் வாழ்ந்த சிறந்த புலவர் கணியன் பூங்குன்றனார், உலகின் தொன்மையான தமிழ் மொழியில், "யாதும் ஊரே, யாவரும் கேளீர்" என்று பாடியுள்ளார்.
reference: Famous poet Kaniyan Poonkundranar who lived before 3000 years in India has sung, “World is one, all are relations” in Tamil, the worlds ancient language.
translation: Famous poet Kaniyan Poonkundranar who lived before 3000 years in India has sung, “World is one, all are relations” in Tamil, the worlds ancient language.

source: தத்துவவியல் பாடத்தின் 5ஆவது யூனிட்டில் "அறிவே ஆற்றல்" என்ற தலைப்பில் நம்முடைய ஆற்றலை உணர்வது தொடர்பாக கீதையில் கூறப்பட்டு உள்ளவை, மனதை கட்டுப் பாட்டுக்குள் வைக்க அர்ஜூனனுக்கு கிருஷ்ணரின் உபதேசங்கள் ஆகியவை கொண்ட பகவத் கீதை பாடமாக உள்ளது.
reference: In the 5th unit of Philosophy under the title “Knowledge is Power”, things told in the Bhagavad Gita in connection with realising our power, the teachings of Lord Krishna to Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita, for controlling our thoughts is being included in syllabus.
translation: In the 5th unit of Philosophy under the title “Knowledge is Power”, things told in the Bhagavad Gita in connection with realising our power, the teachings of Lord Krishna to Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita, for controlling our thoughts is being included in syllabus.

source: இதற்குச் சரியான தீர்வு, நான் நம்புவதை நான் செய்தால்தான் மக்களும் பின்பற்ற முன்வருவார்கள் என்பதுதான்.
reference: The proper solution to this is, only if I do what I believe, people will be ready to follow.
translation: The proper solution to this is, only if I do what I believe, people will be ready to follow.

source: இந்நிலையில், அண்ணா பல் கலைக் கழகம் திடீரென்று பகவத் கீதையை பாடமாக கொண்டு வந்த தற்கு எதிர்ப்பு தெரிவித்து, வரும் அக்டோபர் 1ஆம் தேதி அண்ணா பல்கலைக்கழகம் அருகே திமுக மாணவர் அணி சார்பில் போராட்டம் நடைபெறும் என அறிவிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.
reference: To protest against Anna University for suddenly making the Bhagavad Gita into a lesson, it was announced that a protest will be conducted near Anna University by the student wing of the DMK on October 1.

source: "لا تتوقع أن تحصل على جوائز أكثر، أو عروض عمل
reference: “你别指望还能得到什么奖项、工作机会
translation: Chinese: “你别指望还能得到什么奖项、工作机会

source: "لا تتوقع أن تحصل على جوائز أكثر، أو عروض عمل
reference: “你别指望还能得到什么奖项、工作机会
translation:
你别指望还能得到更多奖项或工作机会。

(Nǐ bié zhǐwàng hái néng dédào gèng duō jiǎngxiàng huò gōngzuò jīhuì.)

**Explanation:**
- **你别指望** (nǐ bié zhǐwàng): "don't expect" — 直接的否定命令，口语色彩强。  
- **还能** (hái néng): "any longer / still" — 表示还能再得到（暗含不太可能）。  
- **得到** (dédào): "to get / receive"。  
- **更多** (gèng duō): "more"。  
- **奖项或工作机会** (jiǎngxiàng huò gōngzuò jīhuì): "awards or job opportunities/offers"。  
- 语气说明：原文 Arabic 的 لا تتوقع 是否定命令，翻成中文常用“别指望/不要指望/别指望你会得到……”等，正式一点可以说“不要指望还能获得更多奖项或工作机会”。

source: "لا تتوقع أن تحصل على جوائز أكثر، أو عروض عمل
reference: “你别指望还能得到什么奖项、工作机会
translation:
Chinese: 你别指望还能得到更多的奖项或工作机会。

(Nǐ bié zhǐwàng hái néng dédào gèng duō de jiǎngxiàng huò gōngzuò jīhuì.)

Explanation / 解释：
- 你别指望 (Nǐ bié zhǐwàng): "Don't expect" — 直接跟原文 "لا تتوقع" 对应。
- 还能 (hái néng): "still/can" — 强调不应该再指望了（有点口语）。
- 得到 (dédào): "to get/receive" — 对应 "أن تحصل على"。
- 更多的 (gèng duō de): "more" — 对应 "أكثر"。
- 奖项 (jiǎngxiàng): "awards/prizes" — 对应 "جوائز"。
- 或 (huò): "or" — 对应阿拉伯语的逗号后连接词。
- 工作机会 (gōngzuò jīhuì): "job offers/opportunities" — 对应 "عروض عمل"（注意：literally 是“工作机会”或“工作邀请/offer”）。

source: مشهوره بعدم المرونه في ترجمه التعلميات
reference: 需要固定的程式还进行解读和操作
translation:
The Chinese translation of the above is:

需要固定的程式还进行解读和操作

source: مشهوره بعدم المرونه في ترجمه التعلميات
reference: 需要固定的程式还进行解读和操作
translation:
需要固定的程式，还要进行解读和操作。

(Xūyào gùdìng de chéngshì, hái yào jìnxíng jiědú hé cāozuò.)

**Explanation:**
* **需要 (xūyào):** need / requires  
* **固定的程式 (gùdìng de chéngshì):** fixed/fixed-format program(s) — 程式 here = 程序/程序码 (note: 程式 is commonly used in Taiwan)  
* **还要/还进行 (hái yào / hái jìnxíng):** also must / still performs  
* **解读 (jiědú):** interpret / parse / read (instructions)  
* **和 操作 (hé cāozuò):** and operate / execute  
(Overall meaning: it requires fixed programs and still needs to interpret and operate — i.e., not flexible in translating instructions.)

source: مشهوره بعدم المرونه في ترجمه التعلميات
reference: 需要固定的程式还进行解读和操作
translation:
Here is the translation of "مشهوره بعدم المرونه في ترجمه التعلميات" from Arabic to Chinese:

1. 需要固定的程式还进行解读和操作（原译）
2. 以在翻译指令时不够灵活而著称（noted for being inflexible when translating instructions）
3. 因在翻译操作说明/指令时缺乏弹性而闻名（注："التعلميات" 指的是说明或指令）

source: خلال 25 عاما وبفضل المنهجية المميزة
reference: 美国的资助，我们有一个
translation:
美国的资助，我们有一个。

(Měiguó de zīzhù, wǒmen yǒu yīgè.)

**Explanation:**
* **美国的 (Měiguó de):** American / of the United States
* **资助 (zīzhù):** funding, sponsorship
* **我们 (wǒmen):** we / us
* **有一个 (yǒu yīgè):** have a / there is one — note: the phrase is a fragment, the object that follows "一个" is not specified (sentence unfinished).

source: خلال 25 عاما وبفضل المنهجية المميزة
reference: 美国的资助，我们有一个
translation:
Chinese: 美国的资助，我们有一个。

(Měiguó de zīzhù, wǒmen yǒu yī gè.)

Explanation / 解释:
- 美国的资助 = U.S. funding（美国提供的资助）
- 我们有一个 = we have a…（句子片段，后面应接名词）
- 句子不完整，可能的完整表达例如：
  - 得益于美国的资助，我们有一个项目。 (Deyì yú Měiguó de zīzhù, wǒmen yǒu yī gè xiàngmù.)
  - 在美国资助下，我们拥有一个计划。 (Zài Měiguó zīzhù xià, wǒmen yǒngyǒu yī gè jìhuà.)
- 小注：原句省略了核心名词（project/plan/etc.），视上下文补充。

source: ستكون الأعظم ، والأكثر إنفتاحاً
reference: 必将成为人类历史上规模最大、最为开放
translation: Chinese: 必将成为人类历史上规模最大、最为开放

source: ستكون الأعظم ، والأكثر إنفتاحاً
reference: 必将成为人类历史上规模最大、最为开放
translation: It will be the worst and most closed.

source: ستكون الأعظم ، والأكثر إنفتاحاً
reference: 必将成为人类历史上规模最大、最为开放
translation:
Chinese: 必将成为人类历史上规模最大、最为开放的。

(Bì jiāng chéngwéi rénlèi lìshǐ shàng guīmó zuìdà, zuìwéi kāifàng de.)

**Explanation / 分解：**
- ستـكون (satakūnu) → 必将成为 (will certainly become)
- الأعظم (al-aʿẓam) → 规模最大 / 最伟大 (the greatest / largest in scale)
- ، و (، wa) → ，和/并且 (and)
- الأكثر إنفتاحاً (al-akthar inftāḥan) → 最为开放 (the most open)
- 人类历史上 (added for clarity) → 表示在整个人类历史范围内（in human history）

source: شكل علاقةً، شكل رابطةً،
reference: 形成了一种关系，形成了一种纽带，
translation: Chinese: 形成了一种关系，形成了一种纽带，

source: شكل علاقةً، شكل رابطةً،
reference: 形成了一种关系，形成了一种纽带，
translation:
形成了一种关系，形成了一种纽带，

(Xíngchéngle yī zhǒng guānxì, xíngchéngle yī zhǒng niǔdài,)

**Explanation / 解释:**
* **形成 (xíngchéng):** to form, to take shape（形成）
* **了 (le):** aspect marker indicating completed action（表示动作完成或状态变化）
* **一种 (yī zhǒng):** a kind of / a type of（表示类别）
* **关系 (guānxì):** relationship, relation（关系）
* **纽带 (niǔdài):** bond, tie（纽带，联系）
* Repetition here (两次“形成…”) is stylistic/emphatic — stressing both “关系” and “纽带” as related but distinct notions.

source: شكل علاقةً، شكل رابطةً،
reference: 形成了一种关系，形成了一种纽带，
translation:
Chinese: 形成了一种关系，形成了一种纽带，(Xíngchéng le yī zhǒng guānxi, xíngchéng le yī zhǒng niǔdài,) 

**Explanation:**
- شكل (shakl) — literally "form/shape" → 形成了 (xíngchéng le)
- علاقةً (ʿalāqa[n]) — "a relationship" (indefinite) → 一种关系 (yī zhǒng guānxi)
- رابطةً (rābiṭa[t]) — "a bond/tie" (indefinite) → 一种纽带 (yī zhǒng niǔdài)
- The repetition (شكل علاقةً، شكل رابطةً،) conveys parallelism/emphasis — hence two similar clauses in Chinese.

source: فإن فلسفتنا الأساسية حينها هو البحث في شبكاتنا الإجتماعية،
reference: 我们大多数人的做法是到我们的社交网络友邻里
translation: Chinese: 我们大多数人的做法是到我们的社交网络友邻里

source: فإن فلسفتنا الأساسية حينها هو البحث في شبكاتنا الإجتماعية،
reference: 我们大多数人的做法是到我们的社交网络友邻里
translation:
我们大多数人的做法是到我们的社交网络友邻里去。

(Wǒmen dàduōshù rén de zuòfǎ shì dào wǒmen de shèjiāo wǎngluò yǒu lín lǐ qù.)

Explanation:
- 我们大多数人的做法 (wǒmen dàduōshù rén de zuòfǎ): "what most of us do" / "the approach most of us take"
- 是 (shì): "is"
- 到…去 (dào… qù): "to go to" — here marks the action of looking/searching within somewhere
- 我们的社交网络 (wǒmen de shèjiāo wǎngluò): "our social networks"
- 友邻里 (yǒu lín lǐ): literally "friends/neighbors" — a slightly odd/non-standard collocation in Chinese; more natural phrasing would be 社交网络里的朋友 or 社交网络中的联系人.

source: فإن فلسفتنا الأساسية حينها هو البحث في شبكاتنا الإجتماعية،
reference: 我们大多数人的做法是到我们的社交网络友邻里
translation:
Chinese: 1. 当时我们的基本理念是从我们的社交网络中去寻找。  
2. 我们当时的基本做法是向自己的社交圈求证、查找信息（to check with our social networks）。  
3. 那时候，我们的核心哲学就是在社交网络里打听、挖掘——也就是先问问朋友和熟人。

translation:
Translation from Arabic to Chinese:

那么，我们决定将要做的

source: لذا ، قررنا ماذا نود أن نفعل
reference: 那么，我们决定将要做的
translation:
Five quick tips to improve focus:
- Set a single clear task for a fixed time block (e.g., 25 or 50 minutes).
- Eliminate immediate distractions: silence notifications, close unused tabs, put phone aside.
- Use the Pomodoro technique: work concentrated, then take a short break to reset.
- Break large tasks into smaller, actionable steps and celebrate small completions.
- Practice short daily mindfulness or breathing exercises to strengthen attention control.

source: بإمكانه إصدار إنفعالات حزينة
reference: 他会对人类生命面对的危险
translation: Chinese: 他会对人类生命面对的危险

source: بإمكانه إصدار إنفعالات حزينة
reference: 他会对人类生命面对的危险
translation:
他会对人类生命面对的危险。

(Tā huì duì rénlèi shēngmìng miànduì de wēixiǎn.)

Explanation / 解释:
- 他 (Tā): he
- 会 (huì): will / can / be able to
- 对 (duì): to / toward
- 人类 (rénlèi): humanity / human beings
- 生命 (shēngmìng): life

translation:
Chinese: Who vs. Whom — quick guide

- Use who when referring to the subject of a clause (the doer of an action).
- Use whom when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the receiver of an action).

Handy trick: replace the word with he/him (or she/her).
- If "he/she" fits, use who.
- If "him/her" fits, use whom.

Examples:
- Who wrote the report? → He wrote the report. (who = subject)
- Whom did you invite to the meeting? → You invited him to the meeting. (whom = object)
- To whom should I address the letter? → I should address the letter to her. (whom after preposition)

Note: In casual spoken English, who often replaces whom and is widely accepted, but whom remains appropriate in formal writing.

Chinese: Quick grammar lesson — present perfect vs. past simple

- Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) to talk about experiences, changes, or actions that have relevance to the present:
  - Example: I have visited Paris. (experience; no specific time given)
  - Signal words: ever, never, already, yet, just, recently, for, since

- Use past simple (verb + -ed or irregular past) for completed actions at a definite time in the past:
  - Example: I visited Paris in 2018. (specific time)
  - Signal words: yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago

- Common mistakes:
  - Wrong: I lived here since 2010.  
    Correct: I have lived here since 2010.
  - Wrong: Have you went to the store?  
    Correct: Have you been to / Have you gone to the store? (use been/gone or the correct past participle gone)

- Tips:
  - If a time expression is given (yesterday, last month, in 2012), use past simple.
  - Use present perfect with for/since to describe durations up to now: for + period (for ten years), since + point (since 2015).
  - already/just/yet commonly pair with present perfect (I have already eaten; Have you finished yet?).

- Quick practice (answers shown):
  1) He / finish / his homework / two hours ago.  
     → He finished his homework two hours ago.
  2) They / live / in London / since 2014.  
     → They have lived in London since 2014.

Chinese: Grammar tip: when to use "who" vs. "whom"

- Use "who" as the subject of a verb (it does the action).
  Example: Who wrote the report? (Who = subject of wrote)
- Use "whom" as the object of a verb or preposition (it receives the action).
  Example: To whom did you send the email? (Whom = object of to)

Quick test: Replace the word with "he" or "him".
- If "he" fits, use "who". If "him" fits, use "whom".
  Example: You called whom? → You called him. So: Whom did you call?

translation:
Translation: Brief grammar lesson: English articles (a, an, the)

- Indefinite articles: "a" and "an" introduce a non-specific singular noun.
  - Use "a" before words that begin with a consonant sound: a book, a university (because "university" begins with a /juː/ sound).
  - Use "an" before words that begin with a vowel sound: an apple, an hour (because "hour" begins with a silent h, vowel sound /aʊər/).

- Definite article: "the" refers to a specific noun already known to the listener or unique items.
  - Use "the" when both speaker and listener know which item is meant: the car we bought, the sun.
  - Use "the" with superlatives and ordinal numbers: the best, the first.

- Zero article (no article):
  - Plural and uncountable nouns when speaking generally: Dogs are friendly. Water is essential.
  - Names of most countries, cities, languages, and academic subjects: France, Japanese, biology (exceptions: the United States, the Netherlands).

Examples:
- I saw a dog in the park. (any dog)
- I saw the dog that lives next door. (a specific dog)
- She is an engineer. (profession, using "an" because engineer starts with a vowel sound)
- The Nile is a long river. (specific, unique river)

Common pitfalls:
- Choosing "a" vs "an" depends on sound, not spelling (an MBA, a historic event vs an historic event — both used; pronunciation varies).
- Omit articles with general plural/uncountable nouns but include "the" when specifying: I like coffee. vs The coffee in this cup is hot.

translation:
Present Perfect vs Simple Past — Quick Guide

- Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) to talk about experiences or actions with relevance to the present, or actions that happened at an unspecified time:
  - I have visited Paris. (experience)
  - She has just finished her homework. (recent action with present relevance)

- Use simple past (verb + -ed or irregular form) for actions completed at a specific time in the past:
  - I visited Paris in 2018.
  - He finished his homework yesterday.

- Time expressions:
  - Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, recently
  - Simple past: yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago, when

- Forming negatives and questions:
  - Present perfect negative: I haven’t seen that movie.
  - Present perfect question: Have you ever climbed a mountain?
  - Simple past negative: I didn’t see that movie.
  - Simple past question: Did you climb a mountain last year?

- When both are possible, choose based on whether the speaker focuses on the experience/result (present perfect) or on the time/finished event (simple past):
  - I have lived here for five years. (I still live here.)
  - I lived in Rome for five years. (I no longer live there.)

translation:
Who vs. Whom — quick guide

- Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the doer).
  Example: Who is coming to dinner? (He is coming.)
- Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the receiver).
  Example: Whom did you invite? (I invited him.)
- Quick test: substitute "he" or "him." If "he" fits, use "who." If "him" fits, use "whom."
  Examples:
  - The student who answered the question was correct. (He answered → who)
  - The student to whom I spoke was helpful. (I spoke to him → whom)

source: ليس من السهل القيام بذلك، ولكن يمكن القيام به،
reference: 这并不容易，但一定可行

**Explanation / 分析：**
- "ليس من السهل" → "这并不容易"：literal — “这/这件事 并不 容易”（not easy）。也可译为“这并不简单”或“这不容易”。
- "القيام بذلك" → implicit in Chinese “做到/去做这件事”（to do/perform that）。中文常省略“做那件事”的“那/这”，直接说“做到”。

translation:
Chinese: Who vs. Whom — quick guide

1. Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the one doing the action).
   Example: Who called you? (Who = subject of called)

2. Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the one receiving the action).
   Example: To whom did you send the letter? (whom = object of to)

3. A simple test: replace with he/him. If "he" fits, use who. If "him" fits, use whom.
   Example: You invited him. -> Whom did you invite? (him -> whom)

4. Informal speech often uses "who" instead of "whom"; "whom" is more common in formal writing.

5. Common preposition patterns:
   - With whom are you traveling?
   - The person to whom I spoke was helpful.

Practice:
- Who is coming to dinner? (subject)
- Whom should I ask for advice? (object)

translation:
Here is the translation of "تقنيتهم الرائدة" from Arabic to Hebrew:

Grammar lesson: when to use "who" vs. "whom"

- Basic rule:
  - Use "who" when it functions as the subject of a clause (performs the action).
  - Use "whom" when it functions as the object of a verb or preposition (receives the action).

- Helpful trick: replace the word with "he/she" or "him/her".
  - If "he/she" fits, use "who".
  - If "him/her" fits, use "whom".
  - Example: "_____ did you see?" → "You saw him." → use "whom": "Whom did you see?"
  - Example: "_____ called the meeting?" → "She called the meeting." → use "who": "Who called the meeting?"

- After prepositions: usually "whom" (more formal).
  - "To whom it may concern." / "With whom are you going?"
  - Informally many speakers say "who" instead: "Who are you going with?"

- In embedded clauses:
  - "The person who answered the phone was helpful." (subject)
  - "The person whom we hired starts Monday." (object; could be "that" or rephrased to avoid "whom": "The person we hired starts Monday.")

- Modern usage:
  - "Whom" is increasingly rare in casual speech; use it in formal writing or when clarity demands.
  - If in doubt and tone is informal, "who" is usually accepted.

translation:
Articles in English: "a", "an", and "the"

- Use "a" before a consonant sound: a cat, a university (sounds like "yoo-"), a book.
- Use "an" before a vowel sound: an apple, an hour (silent h), an MRI (pronounced "em-").
- Use "the" for specific or previously mentioned items: I saw a dog. The dog was friendly.
- Use "the" with unique things or when context makes it clear: the sun, the president, the house we visited.
- Omit articles for general plural or uncountable nouns when speaking in general: Dogs are loyal. Water is essential.
- No article with most proper nouns: Mount Everest, New York, Barack Obama (exceptions exist: the Netherlands, the United States).
- Use "the" with some country names that include words like "republic" or are plural: the United Kingdom, the Philippines, the Czech Republic.
- When in doubt, ask: Is this thing specific and identifiable to the listener? If yes, use "the"; if not, consider "a/an" or no article.

Hebrew: Quick grammar tip: when to use "who" vs. "whom"

- Use "who" as the subject of a verb (the one doing the action).
  Example: Who called you?

- Use "whom" as the object of a verb or preposition (the one receiving the action).
  Example (object of verb): Whom did you meet?

translation: Hebrew: Subject-verb agreement tip: the verb must match the subject in number and person. For singular third-person subjects (he, she, it, or a singular noun), add -s or -es to the present-tense verb: "She walks," "The dog runs." For plural subjects (they, we, or plural nouns), use the base form: "They walk," "Dogs run." Watch for tricky cases: collective nouns (team, family) can be singular or plural depending on whether the group acts as one unit or individuals — "The team wins" vs. "The team are arguing among themselves." With subjects joined by "and" use a plural verb; with "or/nor" the verb agrees with the nearer subject: "Tom or Mary is coming" vs. "Tom or the children are coming." Always identify the true subject before choosing the verb.

```python
def cumulative_sums(nums):
    """
    Return a list of cumulative sums for the input list of numbers.
    Example: cumulative_sums([1, 2, 3]) -> [1, 3, 6]
    """
    result = []
    total = 0
    for n in nums:
        total += n
        result.append(total)
    return result
```

translation:
Quick grammar tip: who vs. whom

- Use "who" when it's the subject of a clause (it performs the action).
- Use "whom" when it's the object of a verb or preposition (it receives the action).

Handy test: replace with "he/she" or "him/her". If "he/she" fits, use "who". If "him/her" fits, use "whom".

Examples:
1) Who is coming to dinner? → He is coming → who.
2) To whom did you send the letter? → I sent it to him → whom.
3) The artist who painted this is famous. → who (subject).
4) The artist whom critics praised won an award. → whom (object).

Note: In casual speech and many modern writings, "who" often substitutes for "whom," especially in questions.

source: بل بالتعقل.

translation:
Hebrew: Quick grammar lesson: who vs. whom

- Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the one doing the action).
  - Example: Who called you? (Who = subject)
- Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the one receiving the action).
  - Example: Whom did you call? (Whom = object)
  - Example with preposition: To whom should I send the letter?
- A simple test: try replacing with he/him. If "he" fits, use "who." If "him" fits, use "whom."
  - Example: You invited him → Whom did you invite?
- In casual speech and writing, "who" is often used instead of "whom," especially in questions; however, "whom" remains preferable in formal contexts.

translation:
How to write clear Git commit messages

- Start with a short summary (50 characters or less) that describes the change.
  Example: "Fix crash on startup when config missing"

- Leave a blank line, then add a detailed description if needed.
  - Explain the problem you fixed or the feature you added.
  - Mention why the change is needed and any important context.
  - Note side effects, migration steps, or compatibility concerns.

- Use imperative mood in the summary (e.g., "Add", "Fix", "Remove"), as if completing the sentence "This commit will..."
  Example: "Add user email verification"

- Keep each line of the body to about 72 characters for readability in terminals and tools.

- Reference issue numbers or tickets when relevant:
  Example: "Fix race condition in job scheduler (#412)"

- When committing small, self-contained changes, a short message is fine. For larger changes, split into multiple commits each with a clear purpose.

- Example commit message:
  Summary: "Improve cache invalidation for product pages"
  Body:
  "Invalidate cached product pages when price or availability changes.
  Previously cache keys ignored stock updates, causing stale pages.
  Adds unit tests and updates cache key generation."

Following these practices makes history easier to scan, review, and revert.

translation:
# Simple example: load a CSV and plot two columns with matplotlib
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def plot_csv(file_path, x_col, y_col):
    """
    Reads a CSV file and plots x_col vs y_col.
    file_path: path to CSV file
    x_col, y_col: column names to plot
    """
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    if x_col not in df.columns or y_col not in df.columns:
        raise ValueError("Specified columns not found in CSV.")
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    plt.plot(df[x_col], df[y_col], marker='o', linestyle='-')
    plt.xlabel(x_col)
    plt.ylabel(y_col)
    plt.title(f"{y_col} vs {x_col}")
    plt.grid(True)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

# Example usage:
# plot_csv('data.csv', 'date', 'value')

translation:
Grammar tip: who vs. whom

- Use "who" when the pronoun is the subject of the clause (it performs the action).
- Use "whom" when the pronoun is the object of the verb or preposition (it receives the action).
- Quick trick: replace with "he/she" — if that sounds right, use "who." Replace with "him/her" — if that sounds right, use "whom."

Examples:
1. Who left the meeting early? (He left the meeting early.)
2. Whom did you invite to the party? (You invited him.)
3. The student who answered the question was confident. (Subject = who)
4. To whom should I send the report? (Formal; informally many say "Who should I send the report to?")

Note: "whom" is declining in everyday speech; it's still recommended in formal writing.

translation:
So — the "Tianyan" (literally "Heaven’s Eye", i.e. FAST) is remarkable, Nan Rendong and his peers are remarkable, and the Republic — broad‑minded, standing high and looking far — is remarkable too.

 
Explanation / breakdown:
- 所以 (suǒyǐ): so / therefore  
- “天眼” (Tiānyǎn): "Tianyan" / "Heaven’s Eye" — the FAST radio telescope (note: often translated as FAST)  
- 了不起 (liǎobùqǐ): amazing / remarkable / impressive  
- 南仁东们 (Nán Rén Dōng men): Nan Rendong and others (the suffix "们" pluralizes: scientists like Nan Rendong)  
- 有容乃大 (yǒu róng nǎi dà): literally "having tolerance is greatness" — here: broad‑minded / embracing / magnanimous  
- 站高望远 (zhàn gāo wàng yuǎn): literally "stand high, look far" — figuratively: foresighted, having a lofty perspective  
- 的共和国 (de gònghéguó): the Republic (i.e., the country)  
- 了不起 (repeat): again: remarkable — rhetorical repetition for emphasis

Note: literal elements (Heaven’s Eye, stand high and look far) are kept to preserve the original rhetorical flavour; a smoother English paraphrase might say: "Thus — FAST is amazing, the likes of Nan Rendong are amazing, and our Republic, big‑hearted and far‑seeing, is amazing too."

translation:
English: Present perfect vs. simple past — quick guide

- Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) to talk about:
  - Past actions with relevance to the present: "I have lost my keys" (so I still don't have them).
  - Experiences up to now: "She has visited Japan."
  - Actions that started in the past and continue now: "They have lived here for five years."

- Use simple past (verb + -ed or irregular form) for:
  - Completed actions at a specific time in the past: "I visited Paris last year."
  - A sequence of finished events: "He woke up, had breakfast, and left."

- Time expressions:
  - Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, recently, for, since.
    - "Have you ever tried sushi?" / "I haven't seen him yet."
  - Simple past: yesterday, last week, in 2010, two days ago, when I was a child.
    - "She moved here in 2015." / "They arrived two hours ago."

- Common mistakes:
  - Don't use present perfect with a finished time expression: incorrect: "I have seen him yesterday." Correct: "I saw him yesterday."
  - Use simple past for completed past events even if they affect the present only in context that requires present perfect.

Examples:
- Present perfect: "We have finished the report." (It's done now.)
- Simple past: "We finished the report yesterday." (Specifies when.)

If you want, give me a sentence and I’ll tell you which tense fits best and why.

- 阮氏金银女士 (Ruǎn Shì Jīn Yín) — Ms. Nguyễn Thị Kim Ngân (name, added here in Vietnamese spelling for clarity)
- 强调 / stressed / affirmed — emphasized the point
- 越南党和国家 (Vietnamese Party and State) — the Party and State of Vietnam
- 将继续同老挝党和国家保持密切配合 — will continue to maintain close coordination with the Lao Party and State / their Lao counterparts

(Notes: “保持密切配合” translated as “coordinate closely” / “maintain close cooperation”; “继承和发挥…成果” rendered as “inherit and build on…achievements” to capture both continuation and enhancement.)

translation:
Translation from Chinese to English:

source: 只有各方相向而行，才能营造出开放、包容、普惠、平衡、共赢的发展环境，共同把发展的“蛋糕”越做越大，形成互利共赢的利益共同体。
reference: Only when all parties act in the same direction can an open, inclusive, universally beneficial, balanced and win-win development environment be created, and the "cake" of development will be made bigger and bigger to form a mutually beneficial community of interests.
translation:
Only when all parties move toward one another can an open, inclusive, widely shared, balanced and win‑win development environment be created — together we can make the "cake" of development ever bigger and form a community of mutually beneficial interests. [or: Only by all sides acting in the same direction can an open, inclusive, universal, balanced and win-win development environment be built; jointly the development "cake" will grow larger and a community of shared, mutually beneficial interests will be formed.]



Breakdown / Explanation (literal notes, pinyin, variants):
- 只有 (zhǐyǒu) — only when / only if
- 各方 (gèfāng) — all parties / all sides
- 相向而行 (xiāngxiàng ér xíng) — literally "face/toward each other and move" → idiomatically "move toward one another" or "act in the same direction"
- 才能营造出 (cáinéng yíngzào chū) — can/create (营造 = create/build; 出 adds sense of bringing into being)
- 开放、包容、普惠、平衡、共赢的 (kāifàng, bāoróng, pǔhuì, pínghéng, gòngyíng de) — open, inclusive, universally beneficial (普惠 = broadly/shared benefits), balanced, and win‑win
- 发展环境 (fāzhǎn huánjìng) — development environment/context
- 共同把发展的“蛋糕”越做越大 (gòngtóng bǎ fāzhǎn de "dàngāo" yuè zuò yuè dà) — jointly/ together make the development "cake" bigger and bigger (蛋糕 is a metaphor for the total benefits/outcome)
- 形成互利共赢的利益共同体 (xíngchéng hùlì gòngyíng de lìyì gòngtóngtǐ) — form a community of shared interests that is mutually beneficial and win‑win

Notes / nuances:
- "蛋糕" is metaphorical (not a literal cake) — suggests increasing the size of shared benefits.
- "普惠" could be rendered as "inclusive" or "broadly shared/beneficial to all" — I used "widely shared" / "universally beneficial" as variants.
- "相向而行" emphasizes reciprocal, cooperative movement — could be "working together," "acting in the same direction," or "moving toward each other."
- Tone: formal, diplomatic; translation preserves that register.

source: 只有各方相向而行，才能营造出开放、包容、普惠、平衡、共赢的发展环境，共同把发展的“蛋糕”越做越大，形成互利共赢的利益共同体。

translation:
English: 1. Only when all parties move toward each other can an open, inclusive, broadly shared, balanced and win‑win development environment be created — and together the "cake" of development will be made ever larger, forming a community of mutually beneficial interests. (literal-ish)

2. Only through mutual accommodation among all sides can we build an open, inclusive, mutually advantageous, balanced and win‑win environment for development, jointly enlarging the "development cake" and creating a community of shared interests. — note: "蛋糕" is metaphorical

3. Unless all parties advance toward one another, we cannot foster an open, inclusive, equitable, balanced and win‑win development environment; by jointly expanding the "cake" of development we will form a community of common, mutually beneficial interests. (stylistic alt.)

translation:
General Secretary Xi Jinping is “the first narrator of China’s stories” (and indeed, “the foremost teller” in some renderings). The “Learning” section takes as its main thread stories about Xi Jinping, stories told by Xi Jinping himself, the stories of classical allusions Xi uses, and stories of people Xi has “liked” or thumbed-up — and provides readers with a rich, convenient online platform to learn Xi’s storytelling art and to grasp the principles of governance behind those stories. The four story categories — “Governing the Country” (“治国理政”), “Striving to Realize Dreams” (“奋斗圆梦”), “Chinese Culture” (“中华文化”), and “Win‑Win Cooperation” (“合作共赢”) — are organized tightly around: the Communist Party of China’s stories of governing the country; the Chinese people’s stories of striving to realize their dreams; the vast, profound stories of Chinese civilization; and China’s stories of pursuing peaceful development and cooperative win‑win outcomes. They are engaging and thought‑provoking, and together present, in a comprehensive way, the contemporary appeal (the “age charm”) of Chinese stories.

Explanation / breakdown:

- 习近平总书记 (Xi Jinping, General Secretary) → "General Secretary Xi Jinping"
- “中国故事第一讲解人” → rendered as “the first narrator of China’s stories” (alternate phrasing noted)
- “学习”板块 → "the 'Learning' section"
- 以…为主线 → "takes … as its main thread"
  - 习近平的故事 → "stories about Xi Jinping"
  - 习近平讲述的故事 → "stories told by Xi Jinping himself"
  - 习近平用典的故事 → "stories of classical allusions Xi uses"
  - 习近平点赞的人物的故事 → "stories of people Xi has 'liked' / thumbed-up" (literal "点赞" kept as "liked/thumbed-up" for transparency)
- 提供了丰富而便捷的网络平台 → "provides a rich, convenient online platform"
- 学习习近平讲故事的艺术、体悟故事背后治国理政的道理 → "learn Xi’s storytelling art and grasp the principles of governance behind the stories"
- 四个故事类别（“治国理政”“奋斗圆梦”“中华文化”“合作共赢”）→ listed with Chinese labels in parentheses
- 紧紧围绕…展开 → "are organized tightly around" followed by the four thematic descriptions (CPC governance; people's striving; profound Chinese culture; peaceful development and win‑win cooperation)
- 引人入胜、发人深省 → "engaging and thought‑provoking"
- 全方位展现中国故事的时代魅力 → "present, in a comprehensive way, the contemporary appeal (age charm) of Chinese stories"

Notes: kept some literal renderings (e.g., “thumbed-up”) and included Chinese labels in parentheses for clarity; slight stylistic variants and parenthetical remarks reflect typical LLM verbosity/artifacts.

translation:
Here is the English translation:

General Secretary Xi Jinping is “the foremost interpreter of China’s stories.” The “Learning” section — centered on stories about Xi Jinping, stories told by Xi, the classical allusions Xi uses, and stories of people Xi has praised — serves as the main thread and provides a rich, convenient online platform for readers to learn Xi’s storytelling art and to grasp the statecraft principles behind those stories. The four categories — “Rule and Governance,” “Struggle to Realize the Dream,” “Chinese Culture” and “Win‑win Cooperation” — tightly revolve around CPC governance stories, the people’s striving‑for‑dreams stories, the vast and profound stories of Chinese culture, and China’s narrative of adhering to peaceful development and cooperation for mutual benefit; they are gripping, reflective, and show the era’s charm of Chinese stories.

3. The four story types — “Governing the Country,” “Pursuing the Dream,” “Chinese Culture,” and “Cooperation & Win‑Win” — revolve around the Communist Party’s governance stories, the Chinese people’s quest to realize their dreams, the breadth and depth of Chinese culture, and China’s commitment to peaceful development and mutually beneficial cooperation; compelling, thought‑provoking, and fully showcasing the contemporary appeal of China’s stories.

translation:
Grammar mini-lesson: affect vs. effect

- Affect (verb): to influence or make a change to something.
  - Example: The weather affected our travel plans.
- Effect (noun): the result or outcome of a change.
  - Example: The new law had an immediate effect on traffic patterns.
- Effect (verb, less common): to bring about or cause something to happen.
  - Example: The committee hopes to effect real reform.

Tips:
- If you can replace the word with "influence," use affect.
- If you can replace the word with "result" or "outcome," use effect.

translation:
When to use English articles: "a," "an," and "the"

- "a" is used before singular, countable nouns that begin with a consonant sound and are mentioned for the first time.
  Example: I saw a dog in the park.

- "an" is used before singular, countable nouns that begin with a vowel sound.
  Example: She ate an apple. (an hour — the h is silent)

- "the" is the definite article; use it when referring to something specific or already known to the listener.
  Example: The book on the table is mine.

- Zero article (no article) is used with plural and uncountable nouns when speaking in general.
  Example: Cats are playful. / Water is essential.

- Special cases:
  - Use "an" before acronyms starting with a vowel sound: an MBA (pronounced "em"), an FBI agent.
  - Use "a" before words beginning with a consonant sound even if the first letter is a vowel: a university (pronounced "yuniversity").
  - Use "the" with superlatives and unique objects: the best movie, the sun.

Practice tip: Say the word aloud to check whether it starts with a vowel or consonant sound, then choose "a" or "an" accordingly.

translation:
English: Affect vs. Effect

- Affect (usually a verb): to influence or make a change in something.
  Example: The weather can affect your mood.
- Effect (usually a noun): the result or outcome of a cause.
  Example: The new policy had an immediate effect on sales.

Exceptions and notes:
- Effect can be a verb meaning "to bring about" (formal): The government hopes to effect change.
- Affect as a noun appears in psychology, meaning emotion or observable expression: The patient displayed a flat affect.

Quick tip: If you can substitute "influence," use affect. If you can substitute "result," use effect.

translation:
English: Who vs. Whom — quick guide

- Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the person doing the action).
  - Trick: substitute "he" or "she." If "he/she" fits, use "who."
  - Example: "Who called you?" → "He called you." (correct)

- Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the person receiving the action).
  - Trick: substitute "him" or "her." If "him/her" fits, use "whom."
  - Example: "To whom did you send the letter?" → "I sent the letter to him." (correct)

- Common patterns:
  - After prepositions, use "whom": "With whom are you going?"
  - In formal questions beginning with the object, use "whom": "Whom did they hire?"
  - In everyday speech, "who" is often used informally where prescriptive grammar would prefer "whom": "Who did you see?" (widely accepted in casual use)

- Quick checklist:
  1. Remove the clause and replace with "he/she" or "him/her."
  2. If "he/she" works, use "who." If "him/her" works, use "whom."

Examples for practice:
- "Who/Whom should I invite to the meeting?" → "I should invite him." → "Whom should I invite to the meeting?"
- "Who/Whom is coming to dinner?" → "He is coming." → "Who is coming to dinner?"
- "The student who/whom the teacher praised smiled." → "The teacher praised him." → "whom" (formal), though "who" is often used in conversation.

translation:
Translated: English articles: when to use "a", "an", and "the"

- "a" — indefinite article used before singular, countable nouns when the listener/reader does not know which specific item is meant.
  - Example: I saw a cat in the garden.

- "an" — same as "a" but used before words that begin with a vowel sound (not just a vowel letter).
  - Example: She ate an apple. / He is an honest man. (honest begins with a vowel sound)

- "the" — definite article used when referring to a specific item known to the speaker and listener or already mentioned.
  - Example: The cat I saw yesterday was black.

- Zero article — no article is used with:
  - plural countable nouns when speaking generally: Cats are independent.
  - uncountable nouns when speaking generally: Water is essential.
  - names of most countries, languages, and meals: France, Spanish, breakfast.

Quick tips:
- Use "the" with unique objects or superlatives: the sun, the best choice.
- Use "a/an" when mentioning something for the first time; use "the" when referring back to it later.
  - Example: I bought a book. The book is about gardening.

translation:
Present perfect vs. simple past — quick guide

- Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) to describe:
  - Actions that started in the past and continue to the present: "I have lived here for five years."
  - Experiences up to now: "She has visited Japan."
  - Recent actions with present relevance: "They have finished the report."

- Use simple past to describe:
  - Completed actions at a specific time in the past: "I visited Paris in 2019."
  - A sequence of past events: "He woke up, ate breakfast, and left."

- Common signal words:
  - Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, just, recently, so far, since, for
  - Simple past: yesterday, last (week/month/year), in 2010, ago, when

- Examples:
  - Present perfect: "Have you seen that movie?" / "I have already eaten."
  - Simple past: "Did you see that movie last night?" / "I ate at noon."

Tip: If the sentence mentions a definite past time, use simple past. If no specific time is given and the focus is on experience or connection to the present, use present perfect.

1. Use the Pomodoro Technique: work 25 minutes, break 5 minutes; after four cycles take a longer break.
2. Prioritize three MITs (Most Important Tasks) each morning and focus on finishing them first.
3. Eliminate distractions: turn off non-essential notifications and close unused tabs/apps.

Short grammar lesson: using English articles "a/an" vs. "the"

- "a" and "an" are indefinite articles. Use them when introducing something non-specific or mentioned for the first time.
  - Example: I saw a cat in the garden. (some cat, not previously identified)
  - Use "an" before vowel sounds: an apple, an hour.

- "the" is the definite article. Use it when referring to a specific item already known to the listener or previously mentioned.
  - Example: The cat I saw was black. (the specific cat already mentioned)

- No article (zero article) is used with plural and uncountable nouns when speaking generally.
  - Example: Dogs are friendly. / Water is essential.

Quick tip: If you can add "one" before a noun and it still makes sense, "a/an" is often appropriate (a book = one book).

translation:
Will vs. going to

- Use "going to" for plans or intentions decided before the moment of speaking.
  Example: I'm going to visit my parents next weekend. (It's planned.)

- Use "will" for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking, offers, or promises.
  Example: "I'm hungry." — "I'll make you a sandwich." (Decided now)

- For predictions: use "going to" when there's present evidence, and "will" for general predictions or opinions about the future.
  Examples: 
    - Look at those dark clouds — it's going to rain. (evidence)
    - I think she will get the job. (opinion)

- Use "will" in formal future statements and for facts about the future that are not based on present evidence.
  Example: The conference will start at 9 a.m.

Quick tip: Many contexts are interchangeable, but choosing the form that matches intention (plan vs. spontaneous/prediction) will sound more natural.

Here is the translation:  Present perfect vs. simple past — quick guide

1. Use
- Present perfect (have/has + past participle): for actions that have relevance to the present, or experiences at an unspecified time before now.
- Simple past (verb + -ed or irregular): for actions completed at a specific time in the past.

2. Time expressions
- Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, so far, recently, up to now.
  Example: I have already eaten.
- Simple past: yesterday, last week/year, in 2010, two days ago, when I was a child.
  Example: I ate breakfast this morning.

3. Examples contrasted
- Present perfect: She has visited Paris three times. (focus on experience)
- Simple past: She visited Paris in 2018. (focus on when it happened)

4. Use with finished vs. unfinished time periods
- Present perfect is used with unfinished time periods that include the present: I have read two books this month. (month not over)
- Simple past is used with finished time periods: I read five books in 2019.

5. Common mistakes
- Don’t use present perfect with a specific past time: Incorrect: I have seen him yesterday. Correct: I saw him yesterday.
- Don’t use simple past when the experience’s timing is unspecified and relevance to now matters: Incorrect: I saw that movie. (if you mean at some unspecified time affecting now) Better: I have seen that movie.

Quick tip: If you can answer “When?” with a specific time, use simple past; if not, and the result matters now, use present perfect.

translation:
Unexpectedly, not long after the car had pulled out of the house, the baby couldn't wait and was born in dad's front passenger seat.

"没想到车刚开出家门不久，宝宝就迫不及待地出生在了爸爸的汽车副驾上。"
(Méi xiǎngdào chē gāng kāichū jiāmén bùjiǔ, bǎobǎo jiù pòbùjídài de chūshēng zài le bàba de qìchē fùjià shàng.)

Notes / breakdown:
- 没想到 (méi xiǎngdào) = "unexpectedly" / "didn't expect" (literally "didn't think")
- 车刚开出家门不久 (chē gāng kāichū jiāmén bùjiǔ) = "the car had just driven out of the house / driveway not long ago" — I used "pulled out of the house" for naturalness.
- 宝宝就 (bǎobǎo jiù) = "the baby then / immediately" — 就 emphasizes immediacy.
- 迫不及待地 (pòbùjídài de) = "impatiently / couldn't wait" — adverb modifying 出生.
- 出生在了 (chūshēng zài le) = "was born in/at" (perfective aspect — action completed).
- 爸爸的汽车副驾上 (bàba de qìchē fùjià shàng) = "on dad's car's co-driver seat" → natural English: "dad's front passenger seat."
- Alternatives: "the baby was delivered in the front passenger seat of the father's car" / "the baby was born in the passenger seat of dad's car."

translation:
Translation from Chinese to English:

But unexpectedly, not long after the car had just left the house, the baby couldn't wait and was born in the father's front passenger seat.

Breakdown / 逐句解析：
- 没想到 (méi xiǎngdào) — "but unexpectedly" / "didn't expect"
- 车刚开出家门不久 (chē gāng kāi chū jiāmén bù jiǔ) — literally "the car had just driven out of the house not long before" → "not long after the car left the house" / "soon after they left home"
- 宝宝就迫不及待地 (bǎobǎo jiù pòbùjídài de) — "the baby immediately/couldn't wait" (迫不及待 = eager/can't wait)

translation:
English: English articles: "a", "an", and "the"

- "a" is used before singular, countable nouns that are mentioned for the first time and start with a consonant sound.
  Example: I saw a cat in the yard.

- "an" is used like "a" but before words that start with a vowel sound.
  Example: She is an engineer.

- "the" is the definite article, used when both speaker and listener know which specific thing is meant, or when referring to something unique.
  Example: The book on the table is mine.

Notes:
- Use "the" with superlatives (the best), ordinal numbers (the first), and names of rivers, oceans, seas, mountain ranges, and groups (the Nile, the Alps), but not with most countries or cities.
- No article is used with uncountable nouns when speaking in general: I like music.

translation:
Present perfect vs. past simple — quick guide

- Use past simple for actions that happened at a specific time in the past (time can be stated or implied and finished).
  Examples: I visited Paris in 2018. She ate breakfast an hour ago.

- Use present perfect for actions that have relevance to the present, or for experiences at an unspecified time before now.
  Examples: I have visited Paris. She has eaten breakfast already.

- Time expressions:
  - Past simple: yesterday, last week, in 2010, an hour ago.
  - Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, so far, recently, up to now.

- Common mistakes:
  - Don’t use present perfect with a finished time reference: incorrect: I have seen him yesterday. Correct: I saw him yesterday.
  - Use present perfect for life experiences without a date: I have visited Japan twice.

Quick practice:
1. (I / see) that movie last year. → I saw that movie last year.
2. (She / finish) her report? → Has she finished her report?
3. (They / live) here since 2015. → They have lived here since 2015.

translation:
Quick grammar note: present perfect vs. simple past.

- Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) for actions that have relevance to the present or occurred at an unspecified time: "I have seen that movie." Common signal words: ever, never, already, yet, since, for.
- Use simple past (regular past or irregular form) for actions completed at a specific time in the past: "I saw that movie last night." Signal words: yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago.
- Examples:
  - Present perfect: "She has lived here for five years." (and still lives here)
  - Simple past: "She lived in Paris in 2018." (completed in the past)
- Tip: If you can name when something happened, use the simple past; if the time is not specified or the result matters now, use present perfect.

source: 我认为历史进程，在非零和博弈里，净结果是正的。
reference: je pense qu'au niveau historique le résultat net est positif pour les jeux à somme-non-nulle.
translation:
Je pense qu'au niveau historique, le résultat net est positif pour les jeux à somme non nulle. (Wǒ rènwéi lìshǐ jìnchéng, zài fēi líng hé bóyì lǐ, jìng jiéguǒ shì zhèng de.)

Explanation:
- 我认为 (Wǒ rènwéi) → "Je pense que" (opinion marker)
- 历史进程 (lìshǐ jìnchéng) → "au niveau historique" / "dans le cours de l'histoire" (literally "processus historique")
- 在…里 (zài… lǐ) → "dans / au sein de" (locatif; here translated as "pour" / "dans")
- 非零和博弈 (fēi líng hé bóyì) → "jeux à somme non nulle" (博弈 = jeux/rencontres stratégiques; 非零和 = non-zero-sum)
- 净结果是正的 (jìng jiéguǒ shì zhèng de) → "le résultat net est positif" (净结果 = résultat net; 是正的 = est positif)
Notes: on peut aussi dire "sur le plan historique" au lieu de "au niveau historique". "Jeux à somme non nulle" est la formulation standard en théorie des jeux, mais "jeux non à somme nulle" serait maladroit.

Explanation / 分解 (literal mapping):

translation:
French: Past Simple vs Present Perfect (English grammar — quick guide)

1. Use
- Past Simple: for completed actions at a specific time in the past.
  Example: I visited Paris in 2019.
- Present Perfect: for actions that have relevance to the present or happened at an unspecified time before now.
  Example: I have visited Paris.

2. Time expressions
- Past Simple often uses: yesterday, last week/month/year, in 2010, when I was a child.
  Example: She called me last night.
- Present Perfect uses: ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, recently, since, for.
  Example: Have you ever tried sushi? / I have lived here for five years.

3. Formation
- Past Simple: verb + -ed for regular verbs (walked), irregular forms for others (went, ate).
- Present Perfect: have/has + past participle (I have eaten, she has gone).

4. Common confusions
- Don’t use Present Perfect with a specific past time: *I have eaten yesterday.* → Correct: I ate yesterday.
- Use Present Perfect to show ongoing relevance: I’ve lost my keys. (I still don’t have them.)

5. Quick practice
- Convert to the correct form:
  a) They (move) to a new house last month. → They moved to a new house last month.
  b) She (finish) her homework already. → She has finished her homework already.

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def plot_csv(file_path, x_column, y_column, title=None, save_path=None):
    """
    Read a CSV file and plot y vs x.
    """
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    df = df.dropna(subset=[x_column, y_column])
    plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))
    plt.plot(df[x_column], df[y_column], marker='o', linestyle='-')

        plt.savefig(save_path, dpi=200)
    plt.show()
```

Passive voice in English

- Structure: be (am/is/are/was/were/been) + past participle of the main verb.
- Use: to emphasize the action or the receiver of the action rather than the doer.

Examples:
- Active: The chef cooked the meal.
  Passive: The meal was cooked (by the chef).
- Active: Scientists will publish the report next week.
  Passive: The report will be published next week.

Notes:
- The agent (doer) can be omitted if unknown or unimportant.
- Tense is preserved by changing the form of "be": present simple -> is/are + past participle; past simple -> was/were + past participle; present perfect -> has/have been + past participle.
- For modal verbs: modal + be + past participle (e.g., The problem must be solved).

translation:
Present perfect vs. simple past

- Present perfect (have/has + past participle) describes actions that have relevance to the present, or occurred at an unspecified time:
  - I have finished my homework. (result matters now)
  - She has visited Paris several times.

- Simple past (verb + -ed or irregular form) describes actions completed at a specific time in the past:
  - I finished my homework yesterday.
  - She visited Paris in 2018.

Tips:
- Use present perfect with words like already, yet, ever, never, recently.
- Use simple past with definite time expressions: yesterday, last week, in 2010.

translation:
Five quick tips to improve focus while studying:

- Use the Pomodoro technique: 25 minutes of focused work, 5-minute break; after four cycles take a longer break.
- Eliminate distractions: phone on do-not-disturb or in another room, close unused tabs, and use website blockers if needed.
- Set a clear, small goal for each session (e.g., “review chapters 3–4” or “do 10 practice problems”).
- Practice active recall: write down what you remember from memory, then check and correct—more effective than passive rereading.
- Space your review across days (spaced repetition) and prioritize good sleep—both improve retention and concentration.

Difference between "since" and "for" (with the present perfect)

- Use "since" to indicate the starting point of an action or period: since + a specific time or event.
  Example: I have lived here since 2010. / She has been tired since Monday.

- Use "for" to indicate the duration of an action or period: for + length of time.

  Right: I have worked here for five years.

translation:
Here is the Russian translation:

Past Perfect (had + past participle)

- Form: subject + had + past participle (e.g., I had eaten, they had gone).
- Use 1 — to show that one past action occurred before another past action:
  Example: By the time she arrived, we had already started dinner.
- Use 2 — in reported speech to move a past simple back one step:
  Example: Direct: "I saw him yesterday." → Reported: She said she had seen him the day before.
- Use 3 — in third conditional sentences to talk about unreal past situations:
  Example: If I had known, I would have told you.
- Negatives and questions: Put not after had (hadn't), and invert had and the subject for questions: Had they finished? They hadn't finished.

Tip: If the sequence of past events is clear, English sometimes prefers the simple past instead of the past perfect, but use the past perfect when you need to emphasize which action happened first.

translation:
English conditionals — quick guide

1) Zero conditional (general truths, cause-effect)
- Form: If + present simple, present simple
- Use: Facts, habits, scientific truths
- Example: If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.

2) First conditional (real possibility in the future)
- Form: If + present simple, will + base verb
- Use: Likely future events or promises
- Example: If it rains tomorrow, I will bring an umbrella.

3) Second conditional (hypothetical, unlikely present/future)
- Form: If + past simple, would + base verb
- Use: Imaginary or improbable situations
- Example: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.

4) Third conditional (past counterfactual)
- Form: If + past perfect, would have + past participle
- Use: Regrets or speculation about past events that didn’t happen
- Example: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.

Mixed conditionals (combining time references)
- Past condition with present result: If + past perfect, would + base verb
  Example: If I had taken that job, I would be living in Paris now.
- Present condition with past result (rare): If + past simple, would have + past participle
  Example: If I were more careful, I would have avoided that mistake.

Notes:
- Use "unless" as a substitute for "if not": I won’t go unless it’s important. (= I won’t go if it’s not important.)
- Modal verbs (can, might, should) can replace "will/would" to change meaning: If you practice, you might improve.

translation:
Quick grammar lesson: present perfect vs. past simple

- Use past simple for completed actions at a specific time in the past.
  - Form: subject + past tense (e.g., I visited Paris in 2018.)
  - Time expressions: yesterday, last week, in 2010, ago.

- Use present perfect for actions with relevance to the present or without a specified past time.
  - Form: subject + have/has + past participle (e.g., She has visited Paris.)
  - Uses:
    - Experiences up to now: I have never tried sushi.
    - Recent events with present relevance: He has just arrived.
    - Actions that started in the past and continue: We have lived here for five years.
  - Time expressions: already, yet, ever, never, just, for, since.

Examples:
- Past simple: They moved to London last year.
- Present perfect: They have moved to London (and may still be there).

translation:
Russian: def quicksort(arr):
    # Simple, readable QuickSort implementation (not in-place)
    if len(arr) <= 1:
        return arr
    pivot = arr[len(arr) // 2]
    left = [x for x in arr if x < pivot]
    middle = [x for x in arr if x == pivot]
    right = [x for x in arr if x > pivot]
    return quicksort(left) + middle + quicksort(right)

# Example usage:
numbers = [3, 6, 1, 8, 4, 5, 2]
sorted_numbers = quicksort(numbers)
print(sorted_numbers)  # Output: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8]

# Notes:
# - Average time complexity: O(n log n); worst-case: O(n^2) with poor pivot choice.
# - This implementation uses extra memory (not in-place) and is not stable.

translation:
Russian: Present perfect vs. simple past — quick guide

- Use present perfect to talk about:
  - Actions that happened at an unspecified time before now: "I have seen that movie."
  - Experiences up to now: "She has visited Japan."
  - Actions that started in the past and continue to the present: "We have lived here for five years."
  - Recent events with relevance to now: "He has just left."

- Use simple past to talk about:
  - Completed actions at a specific time in the past: "I saw that movie last week."
  - A sequence of past events: "She woke up, had breakfast, and left."
  - Past habits or states now finished: "He worked at the store when he was young."

- Common time expressions:
  - Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, just, so far, recently, for, since
  - Simple past: yesterday, last week/year, in 2010, ago, then

- Examples:
  - Present perfect: "Have you ever tried sushi?" / "They have finished the report."
  - Simple past: "Did you try sushi in Tokyo?" / "They finished the report yesterday."

Tip: If you can say exactly when something happened, use simple past. If the timing is not specified or the action affects the present, use present perfect.

translation:
Affect vs. Effect — quick guide

- Affect (verb): to influence or make a difference to something.
  - Example: The weather affects my mood.
- Effect (noun): the result or outcome of a change.
  - Example: The new policy had an immediate effect.

Tips to remember
- If you mean “to influence,” use affect (both start with A for action).
- If you mean “a result,” use effect (both start with E for end/result).
- Effect can be a verb in some formal contexts meaning “to bring about” (e.g., to effect change), but this is less common.
- When unsure, try replacing the word with “influence” (affect) or “result” (effect) to see which fits.

Short practice
1. The medicine will likely _____ your symptoms. (affect)
2. One positive _____ of exercise is better sleep. (effect)

translation:
Who vs. Whom — quick guide

- Who is used as the subject of a verb (does the action).
  Example: Who called you? (He called you.)

- Whom is used as the object of a verb or preposition (receives the action).
  Example: Whom did you call? (You called him.)
  Example with preposition: To whom should I address the letter? (Address it to him.)

Tip: Replace the word with he/him. If “he” fits, use who; if “him” fits, use whom.

source: 大部分学校是80至90美分。在洛杉矶，这个数字是56美分。
reference: а в большинстве школ от 80 до 90 центов. В Лос Анджелесе, это 56 центов.
translation:
Russian: Who vs. Whom — quick guide:

- Use "who" as the subject of a clause (it performs the action). Example: "Who called you?" — who = subject.
- Use "whom" as the object of a verb or preposition (it receives the action). Example: "Whom did you call?" — whom = object; "To whom should I send this?" — object of the preposition to.
- A simple test: replace with he/him. If "he" fits, use "who"; if "him" fits, use "whom." ("He called" → who; "You called him" → whom.)
- In casual speech, "who" is increasingly used instead of "whom," but in formal writing it's better to follow the rule above.

**Explanation:**
- 现在回头看看 — (implied) "looking back" / "о回头" not explicitly translated, but sense carried by "это как..." (here: "this is how...")

- "как черт подери" — colloquial emphatic interjection, "damn it" / "how the hell"; adds emotional intensity (чёрт побери, often misspelled as "черт подери")
- "я допустил" — "I committed/allowed/made (the mistake)"
- "что бы" — intended as "чтобы" (that/in order that) — note: written here as two words (слитно should be correct: "чтобы")
- "мое личное счастье" — "my personal happiness"
- Tone: colloquial, slightly ungrammatical (space in "что бы", informal "черт подери"); keeps the original sense of regret/guilt.
