"Wir sollten die menschlichen Einflüsse auf unsere Ökosysteme fördern und den Schutz dieser Arten nicht priorisieren".

source: "Dieser Bericht zeigt, dass die Lage für viele übersehene und unterschätzte Arten prekär ist, Arten, die das Rückgrat des europäischen Ökosystems bilden und zu einem gesunden Planeten beitragen", sagte Luc Bas, IUCN-Direktor des Europa-Büros. "Wir müssen die Auswirkungen des Menschen auf unsere Ökosysteme begrenzen und den Schutz dieser Arten zur Priorität machen".
reference: "This report demonstrates that the situation for many overlooked and undervalued species is precarious, species that form the backbone of the European ecological system and contribute toward a healthy planet," Luc Bas, IUCN director of the Europe office, says. "We must limit the effects of man on our ecological system and make protection of these species a priority."
translation:
English: "This report demonstrates that the situation for many overlooked and undervalued species is precarious, species that form the backbone of the European ecological system and contribute toward a healthy planet," Luc Bas, IUCN director of the Europe office, says. "We must limit the effects of man on our ecological system and make protection of these species a priority."

(Gloss / breakdown — literal parts and notes)
- "Dieser Bericht zeigt," = "This report shows/demonstrates," (literal: This report shows)
- "dass die Lage für viele übersehene und unterschätzte Arten prekär ist," = "that the situation for many overlooked and undervalued species is precarious,"  
  - übersehene = overlooked, unterschätzte = underestimated/undervalued, prekär = precarious
- "Arten, die das Rückgrat des europäischen Ökosystems bilden" = "species that form the backbone of the European ecosystem"  
  - Rückgrat = backbone; europäischen Ökosystems = of the European ecosystem (alt.: European ecological system)
- "und zu einem gesunden Planeten beitragen" = "and contribute toward a healthy planet"
- ",\" sagte Luc Bas, IUCN-Direktor des Europa-Büros." = ",\" Luc Bas, IUCN director of the Europe office, says." (literal: said Luc Bas — present tense kept as in the clean translation)
  - alt. phrasing: "IUCN's director for the Europe office" / "director of IUCN's Europe office"
- "\"Wir müssen die Auswirkungen des Menschen auf unsere Ökosysteme begrenzen" = "\"We must limit the impacts of humans/people on our ecosystems"  
  - Note: "des Menschen" can be translated as "of man" (as in the clean version) or more inclusively as "of humans"
- "und den Schutz dieser Arten zur Priorität machen\"." = "and make the protection of these species a priority."

(Stylistic notes / small alternatives)
- "effects of man" is an acceptable literal render, but "impacts of humans" or "human impacts" may sound more neutral/modern.
- "Europe office" vs "European office" — both work; many style guides prefer "IUCN's Europe Office."

source: Bei der Bundeswehr verschwinden immer wieder Waffen und Munition - viele davon bisher spurlos. Seit Anfang 2014 verbuchte die Truppe den Verlust von 39 Waffen, 39 Waffenteilen und fast 20.000 Schuss Munition. Das geht aus einer als Verschlusssache eingestuften Auflistung des Bundesverteidigungsministeriums hervor, über die das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland berichtet.
reference: Weapons and ammunition disappear repeatedly from the Bundeswehr - much thus far without a trace. Since the start of 2014, troops registered the loss of 39 weapons, 39 weapon parts and almost 20,000 rounds of ammunition. translation:
Weapons and ammunition keep disappearing from the Bundeswehr — many of them so far without a trace. Since early 2014 the force has recorded the loss of 39 weapons, 39 weapon parts (components) and almost 20,000 rounds of ammunition. This comes from a listing classified as a "Verschlusssache" (confidential/secret) by the Federal Ministry of Defence, according to a report by the Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND).

Explanation / breakdown:

- "Bei der Bundeswehr verschwinden immer wieder Waffen und Munition"  
  Literal: "At the Bundeswehr, weapons and ammunition repeatedly disappear."  
  Notes: "Bundeswehr" is kept in German (the German armed forces). "immer wieder" = repeatedly/again and again / "keep" conveys the ongoing nature.

- "viele davon bisher spurlos."  
  Literal: "many of them so far without a trace."  
  Note: "spurlos" = without a trace; "bisher" = up to now/so far.

- "Seit Anfang 2014 verbuchte die Truppe den Verlust von 39 Waffen, 39 Waffenteilen und fast 20.000 Schuss Munition."  
  Literal: "Since beginning of 2014 the troop/force recorded the loss of 39 weapons, 39 weapon parts and almost 20,000 shots/rounds of ammunition."  
  Choices: I used "Since early 2014" and "the force has recorded" for natural English; "Truppe" = the force/the troops.

- "Das geht aus einer als Verschlusssache eingestuften Auflistung des Bundesverteidigungsministeriums hervor, über die das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland berichtet."  
  Literal: "This emerges from a listing classified as 'Verschlusssache' by the Federal Ministry of Defence, about which the Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland reports."  
  Notes: "Verschlusssache" rendered as "classified/secret (Verschlusssache)" to keep the original term; "Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland" abbreviated as RND in parentheses.

translation:
English: def sieve_primes(n):
    """Return a list of all prime numbers <= n using the Sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    if n < 2:
        return []
    sieve = [True] * (n + 1)
    sieve[0:2] = [False, False]
    p = 2
    while p * p <= n:
        if sieve[p]:
            for multiple in range(p * p, n + 1, p):
                sieve[multiple] = False
        p += 1
    return [i for i, is_prime in enumerate(sieve) if is_prime]

translation:
import random

first = [
    "Morning light on glass",
    "Quiet river bends",
    "Old maps in the attic",
    "Autumn leaves falling",
    "Distant thunder rolls"
]

second = [
    "a soft whisper of wind",
    "shadows stretch and yawn",
    "pages yellow with time",
    "footsteps on cold stone",
    "lanterns sway in rain"
]

third = [
    "memory drifts away",
    "night breathes out its stars",
    "the world holds its hush",
    "a new day opens",
    "silence folds like paper"
]

def make_haiku():
    return f"{random.choice(first)}\n{random.choice(second)}\n{random.choice(third)}"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(make_haiku())

source: Die Bioproben der gesunden Teilnehmer stammen von Hamburgern, die auch bei der "Hamburg City Health Study" mitmachen. Mit 45.000 Probanden ist das nach Angaben des Klinikums die größte lokale Gesundheitsstudie der Welt. Bei der Erbgutentschlüsselung werde streng auf den Schutz der anonymisierten Daten geachtet, versicherten die Wissenschaftler. Es gehe um ein Petabyte (1000 Terabyte) an Daten, sagte Holger Moch vom Universitätsspital Zürich.
reference: The biospecimens of the healthy participants stem from the citizens of Hamburg who are also taking part in the "Hamburg City Health Study". With 45,000 test subjects, this is the largest local health survey in the world, according to the Medical Center. The scientists assure that, in the decoding of the genome, strict attention is given to the protection of the anonymized data. A petabyte (1000 terabyte) of data are involved, says Holger Moch of the University Hospital Zurich.

translation:
Difference between "will" and "going to":

- "Will"
  - Use for spontaneous decisions made at the moment: "I'll answer the phone."
  - Use for promises or offers: "I will help you with that."
  - Use for predictions without present evidence: "I think it will be fine."

- "Going to"
  - Use for planned intentions or decisions made before speaking: "I'm going to study tonight."
  - Use for predictions based on current evidence: "Look at those clouds; it's going to rain."

Examples:
- Spontaneous decision: "I'm cold." — "I'll close the window."
- Planned action: "I've bought tickets; I'm going to see the concert."
- Evidence-based prediction: "The road is wet; it's going to be slippery."
- Promise: "I will call you tomorrow."

Tip: Both forms can sometimes be used interchangeably, but choosing the correct one helps convey whether something is planned or decided on the spot.

source: Noch nie seit Inkrafttreten des EU-Türkei-Flüchtlingspakts im März 2016 seien es so viele gewesen, berichtete der Staatsrundfunk.
reference: Never before have there been so many since the EU-Turkey refugee deal entered in force in March 2016, according to state radio.
translation:
Translation from German to English:

Never before have there been so many since the EU-Turkey refugee deal entered in force in March 2016, according to state radio.

source: Noch nie seit Inkrafttreten des EU-Türkei-Flüchtlingspakts im März 2016 seien es so viele gewesen, berichtete der Staatsrundfunk.
reference: Never before have there been so many since the EU-Turkey refugee deal entered in force in March 2016, according to state radio.
translation:
Never before have there been so many since the EU–Turkey refugee pact came into force in March 2016, the state broadcaster reported.

(Translation note / breakdown)
- "Noch nie" → "Never before"
- "seit Inkrafttreten" → "since the coming into force" / "since it came into force"
- "des EU‑Türkei‑Flüchtlingspakts" → "of the EU–Turkey refugee pact" (or "EU-Turkey refugee deal")
- "im März 2016" → "in March 2016"
- "seien es so viele gewesen" → literal: "have there been so many" (note: "seien" is Konjunktiv I — indirect/reported speech in German)
- "berichtete der Staatsrundfunk." → "the state broadcaster reported." (alternatively "according to state radio" / "reported state radio")

(Literal, slightly more word-for-word: "Never since the coming into force of the EU–Turkey refugee pact in March 2016 have there been so many, reported the state broadcaster.")

English: 1. State radio reported that never since the EU–Turkey refugee pact came into force in March 2016 have there been so many.

3. Never before, the state-run radio said, had numbers been this high since the EU-Turkey refugee deal went into effect in March 2016.

English: Following the record participation last week, it is relatively unclear how big the worldwide response will be this Friday. Thunberg herself was in good spirits. "Last Friday over four million people striked for the climate. This Friday we do it again!" she wrote on Twitter, adding that so far there have been 6,383 actions in 170 countries during the week of strikes (#weekforfuture).

- "Wie groß der weltweite Zuspruch an diesem Freitag nach der Rekordbeteiligung der Vorwoche sein wird, ist relativ unklar." → "Following the record participation last week, it is relatively unclear how big the worldwide response will be this Friday."

  - "weltweite Zuspruch" = "worldwide support/response" (Zuspruch can mean support, backing, turnout)
  - "nach der Rekordbeteiligung der Vorwoche" = "after the record participation of the previous week"
  - "ist relativ unklar" = "is relatively unclear"

- "Thunberg selbst war guter Dinge." → "Thunberg herself was in good spirits."
  - "guter Dinge" = "in good spirits" / "optimistic"

- Twitter quote: "Letzten Freitag haben über vier Millionen Menschen für das Klima gestreikt. Diesen Freitag machen wir es noch einmal!"
  → "Last Friday over four million people striked for the climate. This Friday we do it again!"
  - Note: "gestreikt" literally "struck/went on strike"; English standard past is "struck" or "went on strike" (I left "striked" as a small noise/variant here).

- "Bislang habe es im Rahmen der Streikwoche 6383 Aktionen in 170 Ländern gegeben, ergänzte sie."
  → "So far there have been 6,383 actions in 170 countries during the week of strikes, she added."
  - "Bislang" = "so far"
  - "im Rahmen der Streikwoche" = "in the framework/of the strike week" → "during the week of strikes"
  - number formatting: 6383 → 6,383 (commas inserted for readability)
  - "#weekforfuture" appended as in her tweet/hashtag reference.

translation:
English: Present Perfect vs. Simple Past — quick guide

1. Use Present Perfect (have/has + past participle) when:
- The exact time is not specified and the action has relevance to the present.
- You want to show a connection between past events and now.
- Common with words: ever, never, already, yet, just, recently, for, since.
Examples:
- I have visited Paris. (experience up to now)
- She has just finished her homework.
- They have lived here for five years.

2. Use Simple Past (verb + -ed or irregular form) when:
- The action happened at a specific time in the past (explicit or implied) and is finished.
- You give a time reference: yesterday, last week, in 2010, two days ago.
Examples:
- I visited Paris last summer.
- She finished her homework an hour ago.
- They lived in that house in 2015.

3. Contrast examples:
- I have seen that movie. (You’re saying you have the experience now.)
- I saw that movie last night. (Specifies when it happened; finished.)

4. Helpful cues:
- Present perfect often pairs with: for (duration), since (starting point), yet, already, ever, never.
- Simple past pairs with: yesterday, last (week/month/year), in 1999, ago, when + past tense.

Practice tip: If you can answer “When?” with a definite time, use simple past. If the time is indefinite or related to the present, use present perfect.

source: Aus der Stadt Mansura im Nildelta, wo Demonstranten vergangene Woche Banner mit dem Porträt des Präsidenten in Stücke rissen, wurde am Freitag massive Polizeipräsenz gemeldet. Sicherheitskräfte errichteten Checkpoints in der Stadt und an den Ausfallstraßen. In Kairo wurden mehrere U-Bahnstationen in der Innenstadt wegen "Instandhaltungsarbeiten" geschlossen, die meisten Straßen rund um den Tahrirplatz, dem Herz der Revolution von 2011, wurden blockiert. Und auf dem Rabaa-Platz, auf dem sich 2013 Anhänger des gestürzten Muslimbruders Mursi verschanzten, bis die Armee sie unter Feuer nahm und bis zu 800 Menschen tötete, sollte eine andere Maßnahme verhindern, dass sich Unzufriedene versammeln: Sisis Zukunftspartei wollte ausgerechnet hier eine Großkundgebung für den Präsidenten abhalten.
reference: Massive police presence was reported on Friday in the town of Mansura in the Nile Delta, where last week demonstrators had torn up a portrait of the president. Security forces set up checkpoints in the town and approaching roads. In Cairo, several underground stations in the city center were closed for "maintenance work," with most roads around Tahrir Square, the heart of the 2011 Revolution, being blocked off. And on Rabaa Square, where supporters of the toppled Muslim Brotherhood leader Mursi barricaded themselves in 2013 until the army opened fire on them and killed up to 800 people, another approach was used to avoid the dissatisfied coming together. At this very place Sisi's future party wanted to stage a large event for the president.

translation:
English: 1. Massive police presence was reported on Friday in the town of Mansura in the Nile Delta, where last week demonstrators tore up a portrait of the president. Security forces set up checkpoints in the town and on the exit roads. In Cairo several underground stations in the city centre were closed for "maintenance work", and most streets around Tahrir Square, the heart of the 2011 revolution, were blocked. And on Rabaa Square — where in 2013 supporters of the ousted Muslim Brotherhood leader Mursi barricaded themselves until the army opened fire and killed up to 800 people — another measure was taken to prevent the dissatisfied from assembling: Sisi's Future Party intended to hold a large rally there.

2. On Friday authorities reported a heavy police presence in Mansura (Nile Delta), the town where protesters had ripped apart a portrait of the president the previous week. Checkpoints were erected in the town and on the main exit roads. In Cairo several downtown metro stations were shut for "maintenance", and most roads around Tahrir Square — the epicentre of the 2011 revolution — were blocked. At Rabaa Square, scene of the 2013 encampment by supporters of deposed Muslim Brotherhood leader Morsi until troops fired and killed as many as 800 people, officials took steps to stop people gathering: ironically, Sisi's Future Party had picked this very spot for a major pro-presidential rally.

3. A large police presence was reported Friday in the Nile Delta town of Mansura, where demonstrators last week tore up the president's portrait. Security forces established checkpoints in town and on the access roads. In Cairo several city-centre subway stations were closed for "maintenance work" and most streets around Tahrir Square (the heart of the 2011 revolution) were sealed. And on Rabaa Square — where Morsi's supporters had been holed up in 2013 until the army fired on them, killing up to 800 — authorities sought to prevent gatherings: Sisi's Future Party planned a big rally there.

translation:
1. She was particularly upset that her brother had mentioned Jo Cox, an EU‑friendly Member of Parliament who was murdered by a neo‑Nazi just days before the 2016 referendum on leaving the EU. In the House of Commons Boris Johnson had said her memory could best be honoured by carrying out Brexit. "It's very tasteless to refer to an MP who was murdered by someone shouting 'Britain First'," Johnson's sister now criticised. The attacker apparently came from the far‑right camp, which feels strengthened "by this kind of language." For all who mourn her, it's extremely tasteless.

2. She was especially offended that her brother brought up Jo Cox — a pro‑EU MP who was killed by a neo‑Nazi a few days before the 2016 Brexit referendum. Boris Johnson told the Commons that the best way to honour her memory was to push through Brexit. translation:
In the affair over possible abuse of power by U.S. President Donald Trump, allegations of a cover-up have surfaced against the White House. According to an anonymous informant (whistleblower), several senior government aides reportedly made intensive efforts to prevent access to the verbatim wording/transcript of a contentious phone call between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the end of July. The Speaker of the House, Democrat Nancy Pelosi, explicitly accused the White House of "a cover‑up." Trump called it a "witch hunt."

Explanation / breakdown:

- "In der Affäre um möglichen Machtmissbrauch durch US‑Präsident Donald Trump" → "In the affair over possible abuse of power by U.S. President Donald Trump" (Affäre = affair/scandal; möglichen Machtmissbrauch = possible abuse of power).
- "sind Vertuschungsvorwürfe gegen das Weiße Haus laut geworden." → "allegations of a cover‑up have surfaced against the White House" (Vertuschungsvorwürfe = accusations/allegations of a cover‑up; laut geworden = have been made/surfaced).
- "Mehrere führende Regierungsmitarbeiter hätten sich intensiv bemüht" → "several senior government aides reportedly made intensive efforts" (führende Regierungsmitarbeiter = leading/senior government officials/staff; hätten sich intensiv bemüht = apparently/are said to have made great efforts).
- "nach einem strittigen Telefonat ... einen Zugriff auf die Wortlautfassung des Gesprächs zu verhindern." → "to prevent access to the verbatim wording/transcript of a contentious phone call" (strittiges Telefonat = contentious/controversial phone call; Wortlautfassung = literal wording/verbatim transcript; Zugriff verhindern = to prevent access).
- "zwischen Trump und dem ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj Ende Juli." → "between Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the end of July." (Selenskyj = German spelling; Zelenskyy = common English spelling — both refer to the same person).
- "Das erklärte ein anonymer Hinweisgeber." → "According to an anonymous informant (whistleblower)." (anonymer Hinweisgeber = anonymous source/informer/whistleblower).
- "Die Sprecherin des Repräsentantenhauses, die Demokratin Nancy Pelosi, warf dem Weißen Haus explizit 'Vertuschung' vor." → "The Speaker of the House, Democrat Nancy Pelosi, explicitly accused the White House of 'a cover‑up.'"
- "Trump sprach von einer 'Hexenjagd'." → "Trump called it a 'witch hunt.'"

(Notes: used small variants like "informant (whistleblower)" and "verbatim wording/transcript" to reflect literal vs. idiomatic renderings.)

source: Schon während des Baus hatten die Chinesen mehrfach verlauten lassen, dass Berlin von Peking lernen könne. Die Eröffnung des seit 2006 im Bau befindlichen - und wesentlich kleineren - Hauptstadtflughafens in Deutschland wurde bislang immer wieder verschoben. In Peking dagegen landete schon nach vier Jahren eine erste Passagier-Maschine.
reference: During construction, the Chinese stated repeatedly that Berlin could learn from Beijing. The opening of the much smaller Berlin airport, which has been under construction since 2006, has repeatedly been postponed. Conversely, the first passenger airplane landed in Beijing after only four years.

translation:
During construction, the Chinese repeatedly said that Berlin could learn from Beijing. The opening of the much smaller capital airport in Germany, which had been under construction since 2006, has repeatedly been postponed. In Beijing, by contrast, the first passenger plane landed after only four years.

(Notes / breakdown)
- "Schon während des Baus" → "During construction" (literally "already during the construction"; "Schon" adds a sense of "even while/already").
- "hatten die Chinesen mehrfach verlauten lassen" → "the Chinese repeatedly said/stated" (perfect tense in German; reported speech—Konjunktiv I in original implies reported claim, rendered here as simple past perfect/simply "said" for naturalness).
- "dass Berlin von Peking lernen könne." → "that Berlin could learn from Beijing." (Konjunktiv I "könne" indicates reported speech; translated as "could" to keep the nuance).
- "Die Eröffnung des seit 2006 im Bau befindlichen - und wesentlich kleineren - Hauptstadtflughafens in Deutschland" → "The opening of the much smaller capital airport in Germany, which had been under construction since 2006" (parenthetical dashes preserved conceptually as "and considerably smaller").
- "wurde bislang immer wieder verschoben." → "has repeatedly been postponed" (passive voice; "bislang" = "so far/up to now", rendered as "repeatedly" to mirror "immer wieder").
- "In Peking dagegen landete schon nach vier Jahren eine erste Passagier-Maschine." → "In Beijing, by contrast, the first passenger plane landed after only four years." ("schon" = "already/after only", emphasizing quickness).

(Stylistic note: minor rewording was done for idiomatic English—e.g., "said" vs. literal "had let it be known"—to keep the sentence natural while preserving meaning.)

source: Die iranischen Revolutionsgarden hatten den Tanker am 19. Juli unter dem Vorwurf festgesetzt, Vorschriften des Seerechts im Persischen Golf missachtet zu haben. Sieben der 23 Besatzungsmitglieder waren bereits Anfang September freigelassen worden. Den verbliebenen 16 Crewmitgliedern gehe es den Umständen entsprechend gut, sagte Hånell. Sie hätten sich angesichts der schwierigen und aufreibenden Situation in den vergangenen zehn Wochen professionell verhalten. Die Reederei arbeite nun daran, sie schnellstmöglich wieder mit ihren Familien zusammenzuführen.
reference: The Iranian Revolutionary Guards had detained the tanker on July 19th on charges of having violated maritime law in the Persian Gulf. Seven of the 23 crew members had already been released in early September. All things considered, the remaining 16 crew members were doing well, said Hånell. They had behaved professionally in view of the difficult and stressful situation over the past ten weeks. The shipping company is working toward reuniting them with their families as quickly as possible.

1. Federal Chancellor Angela Merkel has praised the engagement of people in the GDR who took to the streets in the Peaceful Revolution 30 years ago. "In the autumn of 1989, courageous citizens put the then‑GDR regime on shaky ground," Merkel said at a function hosted by the Thuringian CDU group in Erfurt ahead of German Unity Day. She remembered, for example, the occupation of the Stasi headquarters — "State Security was stripped of its capacity to terrify," she added.

source: Die Rolle der Gene beim familiär erhöhten Darmkrebsrisiko ist offenbar bisher überschätzt worden. Zu diesem Schluss kommen Forscher des Deutschen Krebsforschungszentrums (DKFZ) Heidelberg in einer aktuellen Studie. Andere Risikofaktoren wie familiäre Ernährungsgewohnheiten wiegen demnach wahrscheinlich schwerer als bislang angenommen. Das habe Konsequenzen für Berechnungen des individuellen Darmkrebsrisikos, betonen die DKFZ-Wissenschafter.
reference: An increased risk of intestinal cancer through genetic predisposition has apparently been overestimated. This is the conclusion of researchers at the German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) in Heidelberg in a recent study. Other risk factors such as family dietary habits have a larger impact than previously supposed. This is of significance in calculating an individual's risk of intestinal cancer, the DKFZ scientists emphasize.

Try the Pomodoro Technique to boost focus:
1) Choose a single task and set a timer for 25 minutes. Work without interruptions until the timer rings.
2) Take a 5-minute break: stand, stretch, hydrate—avoid screens.
3) Repeat steps 1–2 three more times, then take a longer break (15–30 minutes).
Tips:

translation:
Here is the English translation:

Difference between "who" and "whom"

Rule:
- Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the person doing the action).
- Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the person receiving the action).

Quick test:
- Replace the word with "he/she" (subject) or "him/her" (object). If "he/she" fits, use "who." If "him/her" fits, use "whom."

Examples:
- Who called you? → He called you. → "who" is correct.
- Whom did you call? → You called him. → "whom" is correct.
- The person who answered the phone was helpful. → He answered the phone. → "who" is correct.
- The person to whom I spoke was on vacation. → I spoke to him. → "whom" is correct (formal); in casual speech "who" often replaces "whom": "The person who I spoke to..."

Notes:
- "Whom" is more common in formal writing; many native speakers use "who" in everyday speech.
- If a preposition immediately precedes the word (e.g., to, for, with), "whom" is often appropriate in formal contexts: "For whom is this gift?"
- When in doubt, apply the he/him test.

translation:
English: Quick grammar lesson: who vs. whom

- Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the doer of the action).
  - Test: Replace with he/she/they. If that fits, use "who."
  - Example: "Who called you?" → "He called you." (correct: who)

- Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the receiver of the action).
  - Test: Replace with him/her/them. If that fits, use "whom."
  - Example: "To whom did you give the book?" → "I gave the book to him." (correct: whom)

- Common places "whom" appears:
  - After prepositions: "with whom," "for whom," "to whom"
  - As the direct or indirect object: "Whom did you meet?" → "I met him."

- Informal speech often uses "who" instead of "whom," which is acceptable in casual contexts, but "whom" remains preferred in formal writing.

Quick practice:
- Fill in the blank: "_____ should I contact about the issue?" → "Whom should I contact about the issue?" (formal)
- Fill in the blank: "_____ is coming to dinner?" → "Who is coming to dinner?"

translation:
Scott said he was not surprised by the revelations. They had shown that, in the telephone call, Trump had repeatedly urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to investigate the activities of Democratic presidential candidate and former Vice President Joe Biden in Ukraine. According to Scott, Trump has been watching Biden "for years".



Explanation / breakdown:

- "Scott sagte, er sei von den Enthüllungen nicht überrascht."
  - literal pieces: Scott said — er sei (Konjunktiv I reported speech) — von den Enthüllungen (by/from the revelations) — nicht überrascht (not surprised).
  - natural translation: "Scott said he was not surprised by the revelations." (Using "was" for idiomatic English reporting of the Konjunktiv I.)

- "Diese hatten gezeigt, dass ..."
  - "Diese" = These (the revelations) — "hatten gezeigt" = had shown (past perfect).
  - I translate as "They had shown that..." to keep the same temporal layering.

- "... dass Trump den ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj wiederholt in einem Telefonat aufgefordert hatte, die Tätigkeiten ... zu untersuchen."
  - segments: Trump — den ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj (Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky — note English spelling "Zelensky") — wiederholt (repeatedly) — in einem Telefonat (in a telephone call / on the phone) — aufgefordert hatte (had urged/asked) — die Tätigkeiten ... zu untersuchen (to investigate the activities ...).
  - natural translation: "Trump had repeatedly urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in a phone call to investigate the activities..."

- "... des demokratischen Präsidentschaftsbewerbers und früheren Vizepräsidenten Joe Biden in der Ukraine."
  - "des demokratischen Präsidentschaftsbewerbers" = of the Democratic presidential candidate — "und früheren Vizepräsidenten" = and former Vice President — "in der Ukraine" modifies "in Ukraine."
  - rendered as: "the activities of Democratic presidential candidate and former Vice President Joe Biden in Ukraine."

- "Scott zufolge beobachte Trump Biden 'seit Jahren'."
  - "Scott zufolge" = according to Scott — "beobachte" is Konjunktiv I (reported speech) of "beobachten" = observe/watch — "seit Jahren" = for/over years.
  - natural choices: "According to Scott, Trump has been watching Biden 'for years'." (I used present perfect continuous-ish "has been watching" to convey ongoing action; the original uses the reported-speech mood.)

Notes:
- I kept names in their common English forms (Volodymyr Zelensky) and smoothed German word order into idiomatic English.
- Tense/mood: German uses Konjunktiv I for reported speech and past perfect for the revelations; English rendering adjusts for natural flow while preserving those distinctions.

translation:
Present Perfect vs. Past Simple — quick guide

- Formation
  - Present perfect: have/has + past participle (e.g., I have eaten, She has seen).
  - Past simple: verb in past form (regular: add -ed; irregular: e.g., ate, saw).

- Use
  - Present perfect: actions with relevance to the present, unfinished time periods, experiences, or repeated actions up to now.
    - Signal words: ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since.
    - Example: I have lived here for five years. (I still live here.)
  - Past simple: completed actions at a specific time in the past.
    - Signal words: yesterday, last week, in 2005, two days ago.
    - Example: I lived in London in 2010. (Finished in the past.)

- Negatives and questions
  - Present perfect negative: I haven’t finished. / Has she arrived?
  - Past simple negative: I didn’t finish. / Did she arrive?

- Short practice (answers below)
  1) They (visit) Paris in 2018. → 
  2) She (not/see) that movie yet. → 
  3) How long (you/know) him? →

Answers:
1) They visited Paris in 2018. 
2) She hasn’t seen that movie yet. 
3) How long have you known him?

translation:
Grammar tip: use "since" with a specific starting point and "for" with a duration. 
- Since: "since 2010", "since Monday", "since I met you" — it tells when something began. 
- For: "for two years", "for three hours", "for a long time" — it tells how long something lasted. 
Examples: "I have lived here since 2015." / "I have lived here for ten years." 
When forming the present perfect, combine with "have/has" (I have lived, she has worked).

translation:
Translation from German to English:

Past simple vs. present perfect — quick guide

- Use past simple for actions that happened at a specific time in the past (time can be stated or implied and finished).
  - Examples: I visited Paris last year. She called me yesterday.

- Use present perfect for actions with relevance to the present or when the time is not specified.
  - Examples: I have visited Paris. She has called me (so I know now).

- Key signals
  - Past simple: yesterday, last week/year, in 2010, when I was a child.
  - Present perfect: ever, never, already, yet, so far, recently, for, since.

- For continuing situations
  - Use present perfect for actions or states that began in the past and continue now: I have lived here for five years. (I still live here.)
  - Use past simple if the situation is finished: I lived there for five years. (I don’t live there now.)

- Questions and negatives
  - Present perfect question: Have you seen this movie?
  - Present perfect negative: I haven’t finished the book yet.
  - Past simple question: Did you see the movie last night?
  - Past simple negative: I didn’t finish the book yesterday.

Tip: If you can answer “When?” with a specific time, use past simple. If not, or if the result matters now, use present perfect.

translation:
However, the way Trump spoke about those who are said to have passed the information on to the whistleblower caused outrage. Nancy Pelosi, the Speaker of the US House of Representatives, reacted with concern and complained that Trump´s statement once again undermined the integrity of the government.

Explanation / breakdown:

- "Wie Trump sich in New York über jene äußerte" → "How/ the way Trump (in New York) spoke/commented about those"  
  (Note: "wie ... äußerte" = "how/ in what manner he expressed himself"; "in New York" is a location detail.)

- "die dem Whistleblower Informationen zugespielt haben sollen" → "who are said to have passed/handed information to the whistleblower"  
  (Note: "zugespielt haben sollen" carries an allegation—"are said to have" / "allegedly handed over".)

- "löste aber Empörung aus." → "but caused outrage."  
  ("aber" = "however/but"; "löste ... aus" = "triggered/caused".)

- "Die Vorsitzende des US-Repräsentantenhauses, Nancy Pelosi, reagierte beunruhigt" → "The Speaker/chairwoman of the US House of Representatives, Nancy Pelosi, reacted with concern/unsettlement."

- "und beklagte, Trumps Aussage unterlaufe einmal mehr die Integrität der Regierung." → "and complained/said that Trump´s statement once again undermined the integrity of the government."  
  (Note: "unterlaufe" = "undermine" / suggests it weakens or subverts; "einmal mehr" = "once again".)

translation:
English: However, the way Trump spoke in New York about those who are said to have passed information to the whistleblower caused outrage. Nancy Pelosi, the Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives, reacted with concern and complained that Trump’s statement once again undermined the integrity of the government.

(—literal-ish gloss and breakdown below—)

Explanation / breakdown:
- "Wie Trump sich in New York über jene äußerte" → "However, the way Trump spoke in New York about those..." — "Wie ... äußerte" = "how/ the way ... expressed himself"; "jene" = "those (people)".
- "die dem Whistleblower Informationen zugespielt haben sollen" → "who are said to have passed information to the whistleblower" — note "haben sollen" indicates reported allegation / supposed action.
- "löste aber Empörung aus." → "caused (provoked) outrage." — "aber" here contrasts with preceding context (hence "however").
- "Die Vorsitzende des US-Repräsentantenhauses, Nancy Pelosi," → "Nancy Pelosi, the Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives," — "Vorsitzende" = chairperson/speaker.
- "reagierte beunruhigt und beklagte," → "reacted with concern / was unsettled and lamented/complained," — slight nuance: "beunruhigt" = worried/alarmed; "beklagte" = lamented/complained.
- "Trumps Aussage unterlaufe einmal mehr die Integrität der Regierung." → "that Trump’s statement once again undermined the integrity of the government." — "unterlaufe" here is reported-subjunctive-like (Konjunktiv I) in German, marking reported speech; "einmal mehr" = "once again".
- Small style note: I chose "the government" rather than just "government integrity" to mirror natural English phrasing; both are acceptable.

reference: The ultra-leaders are involved in the illicit trading of tickets, according to Italian media reports. They are supposed to have held the trade of tickets under “military control” and to have blackmailed Juventus employees in order to obtain less expensive tickets.
translation:
English grammar: Present Perfect vs Simple Past

- Use Present Perfect to describe:
  - Actions that happened at an unspecified time before now (e.g., "I have visited Rome.")
  - Experiences or changes over time (e.g., "She has learned French.")
  - Situations that started in the past and continue to the present with stative verbs (e.g., "We have lived here for five years.")

- Use Simple Past to describe:
  - Actions completed at a specific time in the past (e.g., "I visited Rome in 2019.")
  - A sequence of finished events (e.g., "He woke up, ate breakfast, and left.")
  - Habits or states that were true in the past but are no longer true (e.g., "When I was young, I played piano.")

- Common signal words:
  - Present Perfect: just, already, yet, ever, never, for, since, recently, so far
  - Simple Past: yesterday, last week/month/year, in 2005, ago, when

- Examples side-by-side:
  - Present Perfect: "They have finished the report." (time not specified; relevance now)
  - Simple Past: "They finished the report yesterday." (specific past time)

- Quick tip: If you can name the exact time (yesterday, in 2010, last week), use the Simple Past. If the time is not specified or you focus on the result/experience, use the Present Perfect.

- Short practice (answers below):
  1. I ____ (see) that movie three times.
  2. She ____ (meet) him at the conference last year.
  3. We ____ (live) here since 2018.

Answers:
1. have seen
2. met
3. have lived

translation:
English: According to Italian media reports, the ultra-leaders are said to be behind the black market in tickets. They reportedly “militarily controlled” the ticket trade for the supporters' curve and are accused of having blackmailed Juventus employees to obtain cheaper tickets.

Die Analyse / breakdown (literal gloss and notes):
- Die Ultra-Anführer — “the ultra-leaders” (leaders of the ultras/fan groups).
- sollen ... stecken — sollen + stecken = are said to be/be implicated (reported, hearsay tone).
- hinter dem Schwarzhandel mit Tickets stecken — literally “to be behind the black trade in tickets” → “behind the black market/illicit trading of tickets.”
- Sie hätten den Tickethandel ... „militärisch kontrolliert“ — Sie hätten (Konjunktiv II / reported) = they are reported/said to have; Tickethandel = ticket trade; „militärisch kontrolliert“ = literally “militarily controlled” (quoted in original, implying source’s wording).
- und sollen Juventus-Mitarbeiter erpresst haben, um an günstigere Karten zu kommen — und sollen ... erpresst haben = and are said to have blackmailed; Juventus-Mitarbeiter = Juventus employees; um ... zu kommen = in order to get/obtain; günstigere Karten = cheaper tickets.

Alternative renderings: “ultras’ leaders,” “illicit ticket trade,” or “supporters’ stand” for Fankurve — all keep the same basic meaning.

translation:
English: Who vs. Whom — quick guide

Rule:
- Use "who" when referring to the subject of a clause (the doer).
- Use "whom" when referring to the object of a verb or preposition (the receiver).

Simple trick:
- Replace the word with "he/she" (subject) or "him/her" (object). If "he" fits, use "who." If "him" fits, use "whom."

Examples:
- Who is calling? → He is calling. (subject → who)
- To whom did you give the book? → I gave the book to him. (object of preposition → whom)
- The person who wrote this article is talented. → She wrote it. (subject → who)
- The candidate whom we interviewed seemed qualified. → We interviewed him. (object → whom)

Usage note:
- "Whom" is declining in casual speech; in informal contexts many native speakers use "who" broadly. In formal writing, follow the rule above.

source: Hinter den Spannungen zwischen Teheran und Washington steht der Atomstreit beider Länder. Die Amerikaner werfen der iranischen Führung vor, Atomwaffen bauen zu wollen. Der Iran weist das zurück. Die USA waren 2018 im Alleingang aus dem internationalen Atomabkommen ausgestiegen, das den Iran am Bau einer Atombombe hindern und zugleich dessen politische und wirtschaftliche Isolation beenden sollte. Seitdem setzt die US-Regierung die Führung in Teheran mit massiven Wirtschaftssanktionen gegen das Land unter Druck, um ein strengeres und auf andere Gebiete erweitertes Abkommen zu erzwingen. Der Iran widersteht dem Druck bisher.
reference: Behind the tension between Teheran and Washington was the atomic conflict of the two nations. The Americans accuse the Iranian leadership of wanting to build nuclear weapons. Since then, the US government has pressured the leadership in Tehran with massive economic sanctions against the country to force a treaty that is stricter and expanded to other territories. So far, Iran has withstood that pressure.

Since then Washington has pressured Tehran with heavy economic sanctions to compel a tougher, more wide‑ranging accord. To date Iran has resisted that pressure.

In 2018 the United States exited the international nuclear pact unilaterally, a pact meant to prevent Iran from constructing an atomic bomb while ending its political and economic isolation. Since then the U.S. government has applied massive economic sanctions to pressure Tehran’s rulers into agreeing to a stricter, expanded deal (here “auf andere Gebiete” = “to other areas/fields”). translation:
French: Grammar tip — who vs. whom

- Use "who" when the word functions as the subject of a clause (the one doing the action).
  - Example: "Who called you?" (He called you.)
- Use "whom" when the word is the object of a verb or preposition (the one receiving the action).
  - Example: "Whom did you call?" (You called him.)
  - Example with preposition: "To whom should I send this?" (Send it to him.)
- Quick test: replace with "he" or "him." If "he" fits, use "who." If "him" fits, use "whom."
  - "_____ called you?" → "He called you." → who
  - "You called _____?" → "You called him." → whom
- Note: "whom" is increasingly rare in informal speech and often replaced by "who," but it remains correct in formal writing.

The French translation of the above is:

Here's a small Python script that generates the first n Fibonacci numbers and prints them:

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    if n <= 0:
        return []
    seq = [0, 1]
    while len(seq) < n:
        seq.append(seq[-1] + seq[-2])
    return seq[:n]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    n = 10  # change this to generate more or fewer terms
    print(f"First {n} Fibonacci numbers:", fibonacci(n))
```

Explanation:
- fibonacci(n) returns an empty list for non-positive n.
- It starts a sequence [0, 1] and appends new terms by summing the last two elements until it reaches length n.
- Slice at the end ensures correct output for n = 1.

translation:
French: Subject-verb agreement with collective nouns (brief guide)

- Definition: Collective nouns refer to a group as a single entity (e.g., team, family, committee).
- General rule: Use a singular verb when the group is acting as a single unit; use a plural verb when members act individually.

Examples:
- The team wins the championship. (team acts as one unit)
- The team are arguing among themselves. (members act individually)

Tips:
- Context matters — decide whether emphasis is on the group or on individual members.
- In American English, singular verbs with collective nouns are more common; British English more often allows plural verbs.
- With words like "data," "media," and "police," be mindful: "data" is traditionally plural (the data are convincing), though singular usage is common in modern contexts. "Police" is treated as plural (The police are investigating).

Explanation / Détail :
- "Es fehlten bisher" → "ont fait défaut jusqu'à présent" (literally: were missing until now).
- "eine koordinierte Information und Beratung" → "des informations coordonnées, des conseils" (note the pluralisation for natural French).
- "ein systematisches Controlling" → "un contrôle systématique" (Controlling traduit par contrôle / suivi).
- "Ein Einfluss der KEV auf kantonale Verfahren konnte bisher nicht festgestellt werden." → "La RPC n'a jusqu'ici exercé aucun effet notable sur les procédures cantonales." (KEV rendu en RPC; « aucun effet notable » pour rendre le sens de "konnte nicht festgestellt werden").

source: Zugleich regte sie in Form von 13 Empfehlungen an, das Abwehrdispositiv weiter auszubauen.
reference: Le GRECO attend de la Suisse un rapport sur la mise en œuvre de ses recommandations pour la fin octobre 2009.
translation:
1. Parallèlement, elle a proposé, sous la forme de 13 recommandations, de renforcer davantage le dispositif de défense.

source: Etliche möchten diese jedoch erst zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt beginnen: 15'000 Personen (von denen 5'000 an einer Lehrstelle interessiert sind) entschieden sich für die Vorbereitung auf die berufliche Grundbildung.
reference: Certains d’entre eux souhaitaient toutefois ne l’entreprendre qu’ultérieurement: 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées à un apprentissage) ont opté pour une solution de préparation à la formation professionnelle de base.
translation:
Here is the translation of "Etliche möchten diese jedoch erst zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt beginnen: 15'000 Personen (von denen 5'000 an einer Lehrstelle interessiert sind) entschieden sich für die Vorbereitung auf die berufliche Grundbildung." from German to French:

Certains d’entre eux souhaitaient toutefois ne l’entreprendre qu’ultérieurement: 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées à un apprentissage) ont opté pour une solution de préparation à la formation professionnelle de base.

source: Etliche möchten diese jedoch erst zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt beginnen: 15'000 Personen (von denen 5'000 an einer Lehrstelle interessiert sind) entschieden sich für die Vorbereitung auf die berufliche Grundbildung.
reference: Certains d’entre eux souhaitaient toutefois ne l’entreprendre qu’ultérieurement: 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées à un apprentissage) ont opté pour une solution de préparation à la formation professionnelle de base.
translation:
1. Certains d’entre eux souhaitaient toutefois ne le commencer qu’à un moment ultérieur : 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées par un apprentissage) ont opté pour une préparation à la formation professionnelle de base.  
2. Plusieurs préféraient cependant débuter plus tard — 15'000 personnes, parmi lesquelles 5'000 en quête d’une place d’apprentissage, ont choisi une préformation en vue de la formation professionnelle initiale.  
3. Toutefois, beaucoup ont voulu reporter le lancement; 15'000 individus (5'000 d'entre eux intéressés par un apprentissage) se sont orientés vers une préparation à la formation professionnelle de base — (preparatory programme).

source: Etliche möchten diese jedoch erst zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt beginnen: 15'000 Personen (von denen 5'000 an einer Lehrstelle interessiert sind) entschieden sich für die Vorbereitung auf die berufliche Grundbildung.
reference: Certains d’entre eux souhaitaient toutefois ne l’entreprendre qu’ultérieurement: 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées à un apprentissage) ont opté pour une solution de préparation à la formation professionnelle de base.
translation:
Translation: Certains d’entre eux souhaitaient toutefois ne la commencer qu’à un moment ultérieur : 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées par une place d’apprentissage) ont opté pour une préparation à la formation professionnelle de base.

(Literal: Some of them however wanted to start it only at a later time: 15'000 people (of whom 5'000 interested in an apprenticeship) chose preparation for basic vocational training.)

Explanation / breakdown:
- Certains d’entre eux = Some of them
- souhaitaient toutefois = wished / wanted, however (toujours nuance « toutefois » = however/yet)
- ne la commencer qu’à un moment ultérieur = to start it only at a later time (ne ... que = only)
- 15'000 personnes (dont 5'000 intéressées par une place d’apprentissage) = 15,000 people (of whom 5,000 are interested in an apprenticeship/Lehrstelle)
- ont opté pour = opted for / chose
- une préparation à la formation professionnelle de base = a preparatory programme for basic vocational education/training (synonym: « préparation à la formation professionnelle initiale »)

source: Im Vordergrund stehen verstärkte freiwillige Massnahmen, wie die Förderung des Langsam- und des kombinierten Verkehrs sowie der treibstoffsparenden Fahrweise (ecodrive).
reference: On songe avant tout à un renforcement des mesures volontaires, comme la promotion du trafic lent et du trafic combiné et la promotion de la conduite écologique (eco-drive).
translation: Translated: On songe avant tout à un renforcement des mesures volontaires, comme la promotion du trafic lent et du trafic combiné et la promotion de la conduite écologique (eco-drive).

source: Im Vordergrund stehen verstärkte freiwillige Massnahmen, wie die Förderung des Langsam- und des kombinierten Verkehrs sowie der treibstoffsparenden Fahrweise (ecodrive).
reference: On songe avant tout à un renforcement des mesures volontaires, comme la promotion du trafic lent et du trafic combiné et la promotion de la conduite écologique (eco-drive).
translation:
1. Set a single clear goal for each work block (25–50 minutes) and focus on that task only.  
2. Remove small distractions: put phone on Do Not Disturb, close unnecessary tabs, and mute notifications.  
3. Use time-boxing: schedule tasks with fixed start and end times and treat them as appointments.  
4. Break large tasks into 15–30 minute subtasks and celebrate small completions to maintain momentum.  
5. Review and plan every evening: note three priorities for the next day and any quick wins to start with.

source: Im Vordergrund stehen verstärkte freiwillige Massnahmen, wie die Förderung des Langsam- und des kombinierten Verkehrs sowie der treibstoffsparenden Fahrweise (ecodrive).
reference: On songe avant tout à un renforcement des mesures volontaires, comme la promotion du trafic lent et du trafic combiné et la promotion de la conduite écologique (eco-drive).
translation:
French: Au premier plan, on mise sur un renforcement des mesures volontaires, comme la promotion du transport lent et du transport combiné, ainsi que sur une conduite économe en carburant (ecodrive).

(Im Vordergrund stehen verstärkte freiwillige Massnahmen → Au premier plan, on mise sur un renforcement des mesures volontaires)

Explanation / breakdown — quick notes:
- Im Vordergrund stehen — «Au premier plan» / «On met l’accent sur» (literal: “In the foreground stand” → idiomatic FR: emphasis/priority).
- verstärkte freiwillige Massnahmen — «renforcement des mesures volontaires» (verstärkte = renforcées / freiwillige = volontaires / Massnahmen = mesures).
- wie die Förderung des Langsam- und des kombinierten Verkehrs — «comme la promotion du transport lent et du transport combiné» (Langsamverkehr = transport lent / kombinierter Verkehr = transport combiné; could also use «trafic» but «transport» sounds more neutral here).
- sowie der treibstoffsparenden Fahrweise (ecodrive) — «ainsi que sur une conduite économe en carburant (ecodrive)» (treibstoffsparend = économe en carburant; ecodrive left as a term in parentheses).

Alternative phrasings: 
- «On songe avant tout à…», «On met l’accent sur…», or «Au premier plan figure…» — all acceptable depending on register.
- «trafic» vs «transport»: both possible; I chose «transport» to match «Verkehr» in a neutral policy/technical register.

source: Die Herausforderung besteht darin, Bewährtes weiterhin zu ermöglichen und den gut funktionierenden Betrieben ihre Freiheiten zu lassen, gleichzeitig aber Fehlentwicklungen zu begegnen.
reference: L’enjeu consiste à préserver ce qui a fait ses preuves, à laisser leur liberté aux exploitations qui fonctionnent bien, tout en prévenant les dérives.
translation: {L’enjeu consiste à préserver ce qui a fait ses preuves, à laisser leur liberté aux exploitations qui fonctionnent bien, tout en prévenant les dérives.}

source: Die Herausforderung besteht darin, Bewährtes weiterhin zu ermöglichen und den gut funktionierenden Betrieben ihre Freiheiten zu lassen, gleichzeitig aber Fehlentwicklungen zu begegnen.
reference: L’enjeu consiste à préserver ce qui a fait ses preuves, à laisser leur liberté aux exploitations qui fonctionnent bien, tout en prévenant les dérives.
translation:
L’enjeu consiste à préserver ce qui a fait ses preuves, à laisser leur liberté aux exploitations qui fonctionnent bien, tout en prévenant les dérives. (Variante possible : « Le défi est de conserver ce qui marche, tout en corrigeant les dérives. »)

**Explication / décomposition :**
- L’enjeu consiste à… — « The issue/challenge is to… »
- préserver ce qui a fait ses preuves — « preserve/maintain what has proven effective »
- laisser leur liberté aux exploitations qui fonctionnent bien — « leave freedom/autonomy to the farms/operations that are working well »
- tout en prévenant les dérives — « while preventing/avoiding problematic developments/drift »

(La sé-ré-mo-nie ki sə dəʁuˈləʁa ɑ̃ tut ymiˈlite de.byˈte.ʁa a kɑ.tʁəʁə a 14h00 e dyʁ.ʁa ʒys.ka 15h30 ɑ̃vʁɔ̃)  

Explanation / breakdown:
- La cérémonie = The ceremony / the service
- qui se déroulera = that will take place / that will be held (future passive-ish)
- en toute humilité = in all humility / modestly (literally "in all humility"; could also be rendu as "sobrement")
- débutera à 14h00 = will begin at 14:00 (2:00 PM)
- et durera jusqu’à 15h30 environ = and will last until about 15:30 (approx. 3:30 PM)

source: Die schlichte Feier beginnt um 14.00 Uhr und dauert bis ca. 15.30 Uhr.
reference: La cérémonie qui se déroulera en toute humilité débutera à 14h00 et durera jusqu’à 15h30 environ.
translation:
French: La cérémonie sobre débutera à 14h00 et se poursuivra jusqu'à environ 15h30.

Explication / breakdown :
- Die schlichte Feier → La cérémonie sobre (schlichte = sobre/simple/modeste)
- beginnt → débutera (ici traduction au futur pour indiquer un événement programmé; on peut aussi dire "commence")
- um 14.00 Uhr → à 14h00 (en français on écrit souvent 14h00 ou 14h)
- und dauert bis ca. 15.30 Uhr → et durera/jusqu'à environ 15h30 (ca. = circa = environ)
- Remarque stylistique : «en toute humilité» (version plus littéraire) peut remplacer «sobre» si l'on veut insister sur la modestie.

source: Die heute veröffentlichten Zahlen beziehen sich auf das zweite Quartal 2003 (April, Mai, Juni) und betreffen die Luftbelastung – durch Ozon, Stickstoffmonoxid, Stickstoffdioxid, Stickoxide, Schwebestaub (PM 10), Benzol, Russ – und den Lärm.
reference: Les chiffres publiés aujourd’hui se rapportent au second trimestre 03 (avril-mai-juin) et concernent la pollution de l’air – ozone, monoxyde d’azote, dioxyde d’azote, oxydes d’azote, particules fines (PM10), benzol, suies notamment – et le bruit.
translation:
Here is the French translation:

Les chiffres publiés aujourd’hui se rapportent au second trimestre 03 (avril-mai-juin) et concernent la pollution de l’air – ozone, monoxyde d’azote, dioxyde d’azote, oxydes d’azote, particules fines (PM10), benzol, suies notamment – et le bruit.

source: Die heute veröffentlichten Zahlen beziehen sich auf das zweite Quartal 2003 (April, Mai, Juni) und betreffen die Luftbelastung – durch Ozon, Stickstoffmonoxid, Stickstoffdioxid, Stickoxide, Schwebestaub (PM 10), Benzol, Russ – und den Lärm.
reference: Les chiffres publiés aujourd’hui se rapportent au second trimestre 03 (avril-mai-juin) et concernent la pollution de l’air – ozone, monoxyde d’azote, dioxyde d’azote, oxydes d’azote, particules fines (PM10), benzol, suies notamment – et le bruit.
translation:
Les chiffres publiés aujourd’hui se rapportent au second trimestre 03 (avril-mai-juin) et concernent la pollution de l’air – ozone, monoxyde d’azote, dioxyde d’azote, oxydes d’azote, particules fines (PM10), benzol, suies notamment – et le bruit.

(Pronunciation-ish / lecture approximative : Leuh shee-fr puh-blee-ayz oh-zhoor-dwee suh ruh-parrtuhnt oh suh-gohn tree-mess-tre zero-twah (ah-vreel - may - zhoo-een) eh kon-sehrn lah poo-lee-syon duh lar — oh-zon, mo-no-ox-eed dah-zot, dee-ox-eed dah-zot, ox-eed dah-zot, par-tee-kool feen (PM dix), ben-zol, swee no-tahmohn — eh luh brwee.)

Explanation / breakdown (quick map to the German source):
- "Die heute veröffentlichten Zahlen" → "Les chiffres publiés aujourd’hui" = the figures published today.
- "beziehen sich auf das zweite Quartal 2003 (April, Mai, Juni)" → "se rapportent au second trimestre 03 (avril-mai-juin)" = refer to the second quarter 2003 (April–May–June). (I kept "03" as in the original; means 2003.)
- "und betreffen die Luftbelastung" → "et concernent la pollution de l’air" = and concern air pollution.
- pollutants list mapping:
  - Ozon → ozone
  - Stickstoffmonoxid → monoxyde d’azote
  - Stickstoffdioxid → dioxyde d’azote
  - Stickoxide → oxydes d’azote
  - Schwebestaub (PM 10) → particules fines (PM10)
  - Benzol → benzol (note: en français courant on dirait plutôt "benzène", mais j’ai conservé "benzol" fidèle à l’allemand)
  - Russ → suies
- "und den Lärm" → "et le bruit" = and noise.

Small notes / nitpicks (LLM-style aside):
- «PM10» can be written with or without a space (PM10 / PM 10) — I used PM10.
- «avril-mai-juin» is a compact way to list the months; could also be written "avril, mai et juin" for clarity.

translation:
French: #!/bin/bash
# backup_rotate.sh - create a timestamped tar.gz backup and keep only the last 7 backups

SRC_DIR="/path/to/source"
DEST_DIR="/path/to/backups"
KEEP=7

mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
timestamp=$(date +"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")
backup_name="backup_${timestamp}.tar.gz"

tar -czf "${DEST_DIR}/${backup_name}" -C "$(dirname "$SRC_DIR")" "$(basename "$SRC_DIR")"

# Remove older backups, keep only the newest $KEEP files
ls -1t "${DEST_DIR}"/backup_*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | sed -e "1,${KEEP}d" | xargs -r rm --

echo "Created ${DEST_DIR}/${backup_name} and rotated backups to keep last ${KEEP} files."

source: Die Schweiz hat sich an den Verhandlungen zur Ausarbeitung dieser Reformen aktiv beteiligt und das Reformpaket anlässlich der letzen Frühjahrstagung unterstützt (siehe Pressemitteilung vom 9. April 2008[1]).
reference: La Suisse a participé activement aux négociations précédant l'élaboration de ces réformes et a soutenu le train de réformes adopté à l'occasion de la dernière assemblée de printemps (voir le communiqué du 9 avril 2008[1]).
translation: Translated: La Suisse a participé activement aux négociations précédant l'élaboration de ces réformes et a soutenu le train de réformes adopté à l'occasion de la dernière assemblée de printemps (voir le communiqué du 9 avril 2008[1]).

source: Die Schweiz hat sich an den Verhandlungen zur Ausarbeitung dieser Reformen aktiv beteiligt und das Reformpaket anlässlich der letzen Frühjahrstagung unterstützt (siehe Pressemitteilung vom 9. April 2008[1]).
reference: La Suisse a participé activement aux négociations précédant l'élaboration de ces réformes et a soutenu le train de réformes adopté à l'occasion de la dernière assemblée de printemps (voir le communiqué du 9 avril 2008[1]).
translation:
La Suisse s'est impliquée activement dans les négociations en vue de l'élaboration de ces réformes et a soutenu le train de réformes lors de la dernière assemblée de printemps (voir le communiqué du 9 avril 2008[1]).

(La Suisse s'est impliquée activement dans les négociations en vu de l'élaboration de ces réformes et a soutenu le train de réformes lors de la dernière assemblée de printemps — prononciation approximative)

**Explanation / Analyse :**
- **Die Schweiz → La Suisse** : nom propre, traduction directe.
- **hat sich an den Verhandlungen beteiligt → s'est impliquée dans les négociations / a participé aux négociations** : «sich beteiligen an» → «s'impliquer dans / participer à».
- **zur Ausarbeitung dieser Reformen → en vue de l'élaboration de ces réformes / précédant l'élaboration de ces réformes** : «zur Ausarbeitung» = «pour l'élaboration / en vue de l'élaboration».
- **aktiv → activement** : adverbe conservé.
- **und das Reformpaket … unterstützt → et a soutenu le train de réformes / le paquet de réformes** : «Reformpaket» rendu par «train de réformes» (ou «paquet de réformes»).
- **anlässlich der letzten Frühjahrstagung → lors de la dernière assemblée de printemps / à l'occasion de la dernière session printanière** : «anlässlich» = «à l'occasion de / lors de».
- **(siehe Pressemitteilung vom 9. April 2008[1]) → (voir le communiqué du 9 avril 2008[1])** : référence conservée.

source: Die Rückzahlung wird durch die hohen Währungsreserven und den aktuell guten Zugang Brasiliens zu den Finanzmärkten begünstigt und ist Teil einer umfassenden Schuldenmanagement-Strategie, welche auch die Rückzahlung der gesamten Schulden gegenüber dem IWF in Höhe von 15 Milliarden Dollar beinhaltete.
reference: Le remboursement est favorisé par le niveau actuellement élevé des réserves monétaires du Brésil et son bon accès aux marchés financiers. Il s’inscrit dans une stratégie globale de gestion de la dette, qui prévoyait aussi le remboursement complet de la dette du Brésil vis-à-vis du FMI, soit 15 milliards de dollars.

translation:
Le remboursement est favorisé par le niveau actuellement élevé des réserves monétaires du Brésil et par son bon accès aux marchés financiers. Il s’inscrit dans une stratégie globale de gestion de la dette, qui prévoyait aussi le remboursement complet de la dette brésilienne envers le FMI, soit 15 milliards de dollars.

(Prononciation approximative : Le re-mbour-se-ment est fa-vo-ri-sé par le ni-veau ac-tuel-le-ment é-le-vé des ré-ser-ves mo-né-tai-res du Bra-sil et par son bon ac-cès aux mar-chés fi-nan-ciers. Il s’ins-crit dans une stra-té-gie glo-ba-le de ges-tion de la dette, qui pré-voi-ait aus-si le re-mbour-se-ment com-plet de la dette bré-si-lienne en-venrs le FMI, soit quinze mil-liards de dol-lars.)

Breakdown / explication (mot à mot / phrase par phrase) :
- Le remboursement = The repayment/reimbursement
- est favorisé par = is favoured/promoted by; here = "is supported by / is facilitated by"
- le niveau actuellement élevé = the currently high level
- des réserves monétaires du Brésil = of Brazil’s currency/monetary reserves (réserves de change)
- et par son bon accès aux marchés financiers = and by its good access to financial markets
- Il s’inscrit dans = It fits into / is part of
- une stratégie globale de gestion de la dette = a comprehensive/global debt-management strategy
- qui prévoyait aussi = which also envisaged/included
- le remboursement complet de la dette brésilienne envers le FMI = the full repayment of Brazil’s debt to the IMF
- soit 15 milliards de dollars = i.e., 15 billion dollars

(Remarque : "réserves monétaires" peut aussi se traduire par "réserves de change" selon le contexte ; "vis‑à‑vis du FMI" = "envers le FMI" sont des formulations équivalentes.)

source: Die Rückzahlung wird durch die hohen Währungsreserven und den aktuell guten Zugang Brasiliens zu den Finanzmärkten begünstigt und ist Teil einer umfassenden Schuldenmanagement-Strategie, welche auch die Rückzahlung der gesamten Schulden gegenüber dem IWF in Höhe von 15 Milliarden Dollar beinhaltete.
reference: Le remboursement est favorisé par le niveau actuellement élevé des réserves monétaires du Brésil et son bon accès aux marchés financiers. Il s’inscrit dans une stratégie globale de gestion de la dette, qui prévoyait aussi le remboursement complet de la dette du Brésil vis-à-vis du FMI, soit 15 milliards de dollars.
translation:
French: 1. Le remboursement est favorisé par les importantes réserves de change du Brésil et par son bon accès actuel aux marchés financiers, et s'inscrit dans une stratégie globale de gestion de la dette qui prévoyait également le remboursement intégral de la dette envers le FMI — soit 15 milliards de dollars.

2. Le remboursement est facilité par les réserves de devises élevées et par l'accès, actuellement favorable, du Brésil aux marchés financiers ; il fait partie d'une stratégie globale de gestion de la dette qui comprenait aussi le remboursement complet des 15 milliards de dollars dus au FMI.

3. Grâce aux importantes réserves de change et à l'accès solide du Brésil aux marchés financiers en ce moment, le remboursement est rendu possible. Il s'intègre dans une stratégie de gestion de la dette à grande échelle, laquelle comportait par ailleurs le remboursement total de la dette envers le FMI, à hauteur de 15 milliards de dollars.

source: Nur ausnahmsweise sollen künftig öffentliche Gelder an private Ver-anstalter fliessen (Beiträge an zweisprachige Programme in zweisprachigen Regionen sowie an topographisch bedingte hohe Verbreitungskosten).
reference: La commission octroiera les concessions pour les infrastructures de réseau et attribuera des droits d'accès aux diffuseurs privés pour que ceux-ci bénéficient d'un accès privilégié aux plates-formes de diffusion.
translation:
Exceptionnellement seulement, des fonds publics devraient à l'avenir être versés à des organisateurs privés (contributions aux programmes bilingues dans les régions bilingues ainsi qu'aux coûts élevés de diffusion liés à la topographie).

(Pronunciation / gloss)
- "Nur ausnahmsweise" → "Exceptionnellement seulement" (only as an exception)
- "sollen künftig" → "devraient à l'avenir" (should in future)
- "öffentliche Gelder" → "des fonds publics" (public funds)
- "an private Ver-anstalter fliessen" → "être versés à des organisateurs privés" (flow/paid to private organisers; note: Ver-anstalter = Veranstalter)
- parenthesis: "Beiträge an zweisprachige Programme in zweisprachigen Regionen" → "contributions aux programmes bilingues dans les régions bilingues"
- "sowie an topographisch bedingte hohe Verbreitungskosten" → "ainsi qu'aux coûts élevés de diffusion liés à la topographie" (high distribution costs due to topography)

(Alternative phrasing: "À titre exceptionnel, des fonds publics seront accordés à des opérateurs privés ..." )

source: Nur ausnahmsweise sollen künftig öffentliche Gelder an private Ver-anstalter fliessen (Beiträge an zweisprachige Programme in zweisprachigen Regionen sowie an topographisch bedingte hohe Verbreitungskosten).
reference: La commission octroiera les concessions pour les infrastructures de réseau et attribuera des droits d'accès aux diffuseurs privés pour que ceux-ci bénéficient d'un accès privilégié aux plates-formes de diffusion.
translation:
The French translation of the above is:

La commission octroiera les concessions pour les infrastructures de réseau et attribuera des droits d'accès aux diffuseurs privés pour que ceux-ci bénéficient d'un accès privilégié aux plates-formes de diffusion.

(Prononciation approximative : La ko-mi-ssion ok-tro-e-ra les kon-se-sions pour les in-fra-struc-tures de ré-so et a-tri-bue-ra des droits d'ac-cès aux di-fu-seurs pri-vés pour que ceux-ci bé-né-fi-ci-ent d'un ac-cès pri-vi-lé-gi-é aux plates-for-mes de di-fu-sion.) 

Explanation / Décomposition :
- La commission = The commission
- octroiera = will grant / will award
- les concessions = the concessions (licenses/rights)
- pour les infrastructures de réseau = for network infrastructures
- et attribuera des droits d'accès = and will allocate/assign access rights
- aux diffuseurs privés = to private broadcasters/providers
- pour que ceux-ci bénéficient = so that they may benefit
- d'un accès privilégié = from a privileged/preferential access
- aux plates-formes de diffusion = to distribution/broadcasting platforms

(note: small rewording possible — "pour que" ~ "afin que"; "concessions" can also be translated as "licences" depending on context.)

translation: French: Il est par ailleurs examiné si la mise sur pied d'une formation pour les opérations d'information (protection des systèmes militaires de communication et lutte contre le piratage informatique) doit être ajournée.

source: Ausserdem wird beispielsweise geprüft, ob die Bildung eines Verbandes für Informations-Operationen (Schutz militärischer Kommunikationssysteme und Abwehr von Hackerangriffen) zeitlich aufgeschoben werden soll.
reference: Il est par ailleurs examiné si la mise sur pied d'une formation pour les opérations d'information (protection des systèmes militaires de communication et lutte contre le piratage informatique) doit être ajournée.
translation:
1. On examine par ailleurs, par exemple, si la création d'une formation pour les opérations d'information (protection des systèmes de communication militaires et défense contre les cyberattaques) doit être ajournée.  
2. Par ailleurs, il est notamment étudié s'il convient de reporter la mise en place d'un groupement dédié aux opérations d'information — protection des systèmes de communication militaire et riposte aux attaques informatiques.  
3. Il est en outre envisagé, par exemple, de différer la constitution d'un dispositif pour les opérations d'information (sécurisation des réseaux de communication militaire et lutte contre le piratage), question qui fait l'objet d'examen.

source: Ausserdem wird beispielsweise geprüft, ob die Bildung eines Verbandes für Informations-Operationen (Schutz militärischer Kommunikationssysteme und Abwehr von Hackerangriffen) zeitlich aufgeschoben werden soll.
reference: Il est par ailleurs examiné si la mise sur pied d'une formation pour les opérations d'information (protection des systèmes militaires de communication et lutte contre le piratage informatique) doit être ajournée.
translation:
French: Il est par ailleurs examiné si la mise sur pied d'une formation pour les opérations d'information (protection des systèmes militaires de communication et lutte contre le piratage informatique) doit être ajournée .

(Prononciation approximative : Il eh par a-yèr examiné si la mise sur pied d'une for-ma-sion pour les op-é-ra-tions d'in-for-ma-tion (pro-tec-syon des sys-tèmes mi-li-taires de com-mu-ni-ca-tion et lu-tte con-tre le pi-ra-tage in-for-ma-tique) doit être a-jour-née.)

Explication / découpage :
- Il est par ailleurs examiné = On examine par ailleurs / il est en outre examiné (i.e. "it is furthermore being examined")
- si = if / whether
- la mise sur pied = la création / la mise en place (establishment, setting-up)
- d'une formation = d'une unité/formation (here: a formation/training or a unit/structure)
- pour les opérations d'information = destinée aux opérations d'information (information operations)
- (protection des systèmes militaires de communication et lutte contre le piratage informatique) = précision/exemple : protection des réseaux/ systèmes de communication militaires et défense contre les attaques de hackers
- doit être ajournée = devrait être reportée / mise en attente (should be postponed)

reference: La Suisse compte environ 6 % d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.
translation: La Suisse compte environ 6 % d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.??

source: Im europäischen Vergleich liegt die Schweiz hinsichtlich des Anteils der Studierenden mit Kind mit rund 6% im Mittelfeld.
reference: La Suisse compte environ 6 % d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.
translation:
La Suisse compte environ 6 % d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.

(La Suisse compte environ six pour cent d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.)

**Explanation / Breakdown:**
- La Suisse = Switzerland
- compte = counts/has
- environ 6 % = about 6 percent (note the non-breaking space before % typical in French)
- d’étudiants avec enfant à charge = of students with a (dependent) child / students who have a child to support
- ce qui la situe = which places it / which puts it
- en milieu de classement = in the middle of the ranking / mid-table
- en comparaison européenne = in European comparison / compared to other European countries

(Minor note: you might also see "ayant un enfant à charge" instead of "avec enfant à charge" — both are acceptable; the phrasing here mirrors the source structure.)

source: Im europäischen Vergleich liegt die Schweiz hinsichtlich des Anteils der Studierenden mit Kind mit rund 6% im Mittelfeld.
reference: La Suisse compte environ 6 % d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.
translation:
French: 1. La Suisse compte environ 6 % d’étudiants avec enfant à charge, ce qui la situe en milieu de classement en comparaison européenne.
2. En comparaison européenne, la Suisse se situe au milieu du peloton avec environ 6 % d’étudiants ayant un enfant à charge — soit un taux d’à peu près 6 %.
3. La Suisse, avec près de 6 % d'étudiants parents (étudiants ayant un enfant), se trouve dans la moyenne européenne.

translation:
French: Tip: Unterschiede zwischen "its" und "it's" im Englischen

- "its" ist ein Possessivpronomen und zeigt Besitz an.
  Beispiel: The cat licked its paw.

- "it's" ist eine Kontraktion von "it is" oder "it has".
  Beispiele: It's raining. / It's been a long day.

Merktipp: Wenn du "it is" oder "it has" einsetzen kannst, schreibe "it's". Wenn du Besitz ausdrücken möchtest, benutze "its".

translation:
French: Common English phrasal verbs with "get" and how to use them:

- get up — to rise from bed or a sitting position
  Example: I usually get up at 7 a.m.

- get along (with) — to have a good relationship
  Example: She gets along with all her coworkers.

- get by — to manage or survive, especially with difficulty
  Example: We don’t earn much, but we get by.

- get over — to recover from something (illness, breakup, shock)
  Example: It took him months to get over the breakup.

- get rid of — to eliminate or dispose of something
  Example: I need to get rid of these old magazines.

- get together — to meet or gather socially
  Example: Let’s get together this weekend for dinner.

Tips:
- Phrasal verbs can be separable or inseparable; practice with examples to learn which is which.
- Many phrasal verbs have multiple meanings depending on context.

Mit der Kontingentfreigabe für Erwerbstätige aus Drittstaaten stellt der Bundesrat der Wirtschaft für das kommende Jahr die nötige Anzahl Bewilligungen für qualifizierte Fachkräfte zur Verfügung.

Français: En 2012, les entreprises suisses pourront recruter au total 8'500 spécialistes en provenance d'États tiers (3'500 autorisations de séjour et 5'000 autorisations de séjour de courte durée). Par la libération d'un contingent pour les personnes actives originaires de pays tiers, le Conseil fédéral met à la disposition des milieux économiques, pour l'année à venir, le nombre nécessaire d'autorisations permettant l'arrivée en Suisse de travailleurs qualifiés. (variante: «permis de séjour» / «autorisations temporaires» — formulation possible).  

Note (English): Swiss number format often uses apostrophes (8'500) — sometimes written 8 500.

source: Die Schweizer Unternehmen können 2012 insgesamt 8'500 Spezialistinnen und Spezialisten aus Drittstaaten rekrutieren (3'500 Aufenthaltsbewilligungen und 5'000 Kurzaufenthaltsbewilligungen). Mit der Kontingentfreigabe für Erwerbstätige aus Drittstaaten stellt der Bundesrat der Wirtschaft für das kommende Jahr die nötige Anzahl Bewilligungen für qualifizierte Fachkräfte zur Verfügung.
reference: En 2012, elles pourront recruter au total 8500 spécialistes en provenance d'États tiers (3500 autorisations de séjour et 5000 autorisations de séjour de courte durée). Le Conseil fédéral met ainsi à la disposition des milieux économiques le nombre nécessaire d'autorisations pour permettre la venue en Suisse en 2012 de travailleurs qualifiés en provenance d'Etats tiers.
translation: French: In 2012 Swiss companies can recruit a total of 85,000 specialists from third countries (3,500 residence permits and 5,000 short-stay permits). By releasing the quota for workers from third countries, the Federal Council supplies the economy with the necessary number of permits for unqualified labor for the coming year.

source: Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (BFS) - Nach den provisorischen Ergebnissen des Bundesamtes für Statistik (BFS) sind die realen, saisonbereinigten Detailhandelsumsätze im Februar 2010 gegenüber Januar 2010 um 0,6 Prozent gestiegen (nominal +0,3%).
reference: Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (OFS) - Selon les résultats provisoires de l'Office fédéral de la statistique (OFS), les chiffres d'affaires du commerce de détail ajustés des variations saisonnières ont augmenté de 0,6% en termes réels en février 2010 par rapport à janvier 2010 (+0,3% en termes nominaux).
translation:
The French translation of the above is:

Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (OFS) - Selon les résultats provisoires de l'Office fédéral de la statistique (OFS), les chiffres d'affaires du commerce de détail ajustés des variations saisonnières ont augmenté de 0,6% en termes réels en février 2010 par rapport à janvier 2010 (+0,3% en termes nominaux).

source: Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (BFS) - Nach den provisorischen Ergebnissen des Bundesamtes für Statistik (BFS) sind die realen, saisonbereinigten Detailhandelsumsätze im Februar 2010 gegenüber Januar 2010 um 0,6 Prozent gestiegen (nominal +0,3%).
reference: Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (OFS) - Selon les résultats provisoires de l'Office fédéral de la statistique (OFS), les chiffres d'affaires du commerce de détail ajustés des variations saisonnières ont augmenté de 0,6% en termes réels en février 2010 par rapport à janvier 2010 (+0,3% en termes nominaux).
translation:
Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (OFS/BFS) - Selon les résultats provisoires de l'Office fédéral de la statistique (OFS), les chiffres d'affaires du commerce de détail, ajustés des variations saisonnières, ont augmenté de 0,6 % en termes réels en février 2010 par rapport à janvier 2010 (+0,3 % en termes nominaux).

(Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 - (OFS/BFS) - Selon les rés. provisoires de l'Office féd. de la statistique (OFS), les CA du comm. de détail, ajustés saisonnièrement, ont +0,6 % réels en fév. 2010 vs jan. 2010 (+0,3 % nomin.).)

Explanation / breakdown:
- Neuchâtel, 07.04.2010 : lieu et date — same as source.
- (OFS/BFS) : j'ai gardé les deux sigles (OFS = Office fédéral de la statistique, BFS = Bundesamt für Statistik) pour refléter la version allemande.
- Selon les résultats provisoires de l'Office fédéral de la statistique (OFS) : “According to the provisional results of the Federal Statistical Office”.
- les chiffres d'affaires du commerce de détail : “retail turnover/sales” (plural to match German Umsätze).
- ajustés des variations saisonnières / corrigés des variations saisonnières : “seasonally adjusted”.
- ont augmenté de 0,6 % en termes réels : “increased by 0.6 percent in real terms”.
- par rapport à janvier 2010 (+0,3 % en termes nominaux) : “compared with January 2010 (+0.3% in nominal terms)”.

Small notes (noise): abbr. and minor contractions added in the parenthetical line to mimic an LLM's compact restatement; meaning preserved.
